Adds [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) as a SpecStory CLI provider, updated from #156 by @marton78 (thank you!).

OpenCode 2.0 replaced the JSON `storage/` tree #156 was written against with a single SQLite database owned by a background service, so the provider was rebuilt on the 2.x store. The original commits remain in this branch's history.

## What it supports

- `sync`, `run`, `watch`, `list`, `search`/`reindex`, `check`, `--debug-raw`
- `resume` in both directions: OpenCode sessions into other agents, and any agent's session into OpenCode (staged as an OpenCode export document and loaded with `opencode session import`, so OpenCode assigns project ids and sequences itself)
- Every message kind in OpenCode 2.0.14's schema is handled: user prompts, assistant steps (text, reasoning, tool parts), user `!` shell commands, compaction summaries; scaffolding and lifecycle records are skipped with a logged reason
- Bespoke rendering for every declared tool (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `shell`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `skill`, `subagent`, `execute`, `question`), each traced to observed records
- Factory scripts: `latest-version` (npm `@opencode/cli` latest), `install` (vendor 2.x installer, pinned), `list-tools`

Format reference: [`OPENCODE-FORMAT.md`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/OPENCODE-FORMAT.md)

## Tested against

- OpenCode `opencode v2.0.14` (the version floor in the changelog; replace with the release-day version)
- macOS 26.6.2 (Darwin 25.6.0 arm64). Linux and native Windows were not run against the real agent; the unit tests run on Windows in CI, and `GOOS=windows go build/vet ./...` pass locally.

## Evidence

- Command matrix, every row of the guide's table: [`examples/MANUAL-TESTS.md`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/examples/MANUAL-TESTS.md)
- Tool audit, all 32 calls in three captured sessions graded against their native records: [`examples/TOOL-AUDIT.md`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/examples/TOOL-AUDIT.md)
- [`tools.txt`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/testdata/tools.txt) (in `testdata/` because the inventory sweep test reads it), [`versions.txt`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/examples/versions.txt), rendered histories: [`tool-exercise.md`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/examples/tool-exercise.md), [`optional-params.md`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/examples/optional-params.md), [`question.md`](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/blob/opencode-provider/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/opencode/examples/question.md)
- Tests use real sessions captured from OpenCode 2.0.14 (paths neutralized) loaded into a database built from OpenCode's own DDL; every watcher acceptance case has its own test, and each regression test was checked to fail without its fix.

## Review hand-back (per docs/NEW-PROVIDER-REVIEW.md)

**Scope.** Reviewed revision: the branch head (`9d193ed`), compared with `dev`; no uncommitted work except `.specstory/history` files. Agent: OpenCode `opencode v2.0.14`; store: one SQLite database (`opencode.db`, WAL) owned by OpenCode's background service. Capabilities: all SPI methods including reconstruction, plus `ProgressEnumerator`; `PathSessionReader` deliberately not implemented (one database file for all sessions). The contribution's 1.x implementation was stale against both the SPI (6 missing/changed methods) and OpenCode (storage format replaced in 2.0); it was replaced rather than patched, so integration gaps and provider defects were not separated further.

**Decision: ready to merge**, pending the maintainer's release follow-ups below. No open blocking findings.

**Verification, by method**
- Code inspection: every SPI method and wiring point against the guide and its self-review checklist; `/pr-review 330` run and its findings fixed (387a860); forbidden-pattern scan (no `fmt.Print`, `os.Exit`, `wg.Add`, bare `err ==` comparisons, literal fences, or imports of `pkg/utils`/`session`/`cloud`/`telemetry`).
- Fixture placement: every `testdata/` file has an automated consumer (`schema.sql` → fixture database; `tool-exercise`, `tui-session`, `optional-params`, `model-error`, `question` `.jsonl` → conversion, rendering and provider tests; `tools.txt` → inventory sweep, moved from `examples/` in 177eb2d); nothing under `examples/` is read by a test.
- Automated: `go test ./...`, race runs of the watcher tests, `golangci-lint run`, `GOOS=windows go build/vet ./...`; CI (Lint, Test, Test (Windows), CodeQL) green on the reviewed head.
- Real agent (macOS only): every row of the guide's command matrix, both cross-agent resume directions, symlink/space paths; see `examples/MANUAL-TESTS.md` and `examples/TOOL-AUDIT.md`.
- Untested: Linux and native Windows against the real agent; the `websearch` success path (no search provider available); `patch` (not offered to the models available); a real attachment-only prompt (covered by a schema-shaped guard test).

**Findings fixed during review** (numbered for discussion)
1. Stale implementation: 1.x JSON store and 6 SPI gaps → provider rebuilt on the 2.x SQLite store.
2. Reindex could skip changed sessions of WAL-backed stores (`pkg/cmd/reindex.go` `statNative`) → WAL folded into the fingerprint; also fixes Cursor IDE. Shared change.
3. Watcher startup baseline taken once could republish history after a failed first read → boundary applied on first sight of every session.
4. Reconstructed transcripts staged world-readable under a shared temp dir → per-user cache dir, 0700.
5. `--project-path` runs launched OpenCode in the caller's directory → launched in the project.
6. Attachment-only prompts left a session unnamed and unsynced → shared naming rule for listing and conversion.
7. Step errors could sort before the parts that preceded them → carried-forward timestamp, regression test.
8. `list-tools` accepted a failed agent run → any non-zero exit fails.
9. Windows fixture writes raced the watcher's reads (SQLITE_BUSY) → busy timeout on the fixture writer.
10. Consumed `tools.txt` lived in `examples/` → moved to `testdata/`.
11. Any stat error at watcher startup (not only a missing database) adopted every session → only a missing store is adopted.
12. A session of `!` shell commands only was dropped (no naming prompt) → named by its first command in listing and conversion.
13. `list-tools` accepted a self-report naming only read and shell → all six core tools required.
14. A store created or restored while the watcher was starting was classed as pre-existing and its older sessions baselined → existence decided before the startup boundary.

**Release follow-ups (not merge blockers)**
- Changelog: replace the `2.0.14` version floor with the release-day version and move the entry under the release heading; fill in the root README Min Version.
- Website documentation for OpenCode.
- Factory enrollment: `latest-version`, `install`, and `list-tools` with `OPENCODE_FACTORY_MODEL=opencode/big-pickle`.

## Shared-code changes

- `pkg/cmd/reindex.go` `statNative`: folds a `<path>-wal` sibling's size and mtime into the reindex fingerprint. For a SQLite store in WAL mode (OpenCode, and Cursor IDE's `state.vscdb`) commits land in the WAL until a checkpoint, so an incremental reindex could skip a changed session. Paths without a `-wal` file keep their fingerprint; the first reindex after upgrading re-reads WAL-backed sessions once.
- Config wiring (`opencode_cmd`), registry, TUI color, both READMEs, changelog draft under `## Unreleased`.

## Known limitations

- OpenCode stores an expanded slash command (e.g. `/review`) as a plain user record with no command marker, so the template text renders as the prompt and is replayed when resumed into another agent.
- OpenCode's free Zen models refuse to continue history that was not produced through Zen (HTTP 403, "free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"); a session resumed into OpenCode needs another configured model. Verified with Fireworks.
- `opencode run -s <id>` stalls on the first prompt into a freshly imported session; the TUI that `specstory resume` launches is unaffected.
- `specstory resume --session <id>` accepts only UUID-shaped ids (shared CLI parsing), so OpenCode's `ses_...` ids work through the picker but not that flag.
- `list-tools` asks the model (`OPENCODE_FACTORY_MODEL`): 2.0.14 exposes no harness tool declaration.

## Review

- `/pr-review 330` was run; its actionable findings (error ordering within a failed step, watcher delivering while the database was open, staging directory created on every resume, stale comments, duplicated lookups) are fixed in 387a860. The duplicated shell-output sanitizer (now in Pi, Muse Code and OpenCode) is left as a follow-up to promote into `pkg/spi`.
- Copilot findings were triaged in-thread: accepted ones fixed (private staging directory, launch directory for `--project-path`, attachment-only prompts, WAL-aware reindex), the rest answered with the evidence (neutral reconstruction agent, nil-safe scan reporter, outdated threads on the replaced 1.x code).

## Follow-ups outside this PR

- Claude Code provider: `isMeta` user records (e.g. Claude Code 2.1.280's markdown copy of `/context` output) are rendered and replayed as user prompts.
- `specstory resume` blocks while a provider's `Check` hangs (`agy --version` hung during testing); checks have no timeout.
- `pkg/providers/cursoride/database.go` opens `?mode=ro` without the `file:` scheme, so the driver ignores read-only mode.
- Windows CI flake: the Cursor CLI (`watcher_test.go:197`) and Grok Build (`watcher_test.go:461`) watcher tests hit the 5-minute timeout once on dddf533 and passed on re-run; neither package is changed here.
- Migration note grammar: "Resumed from a OpenCode session".
- Release: version floor and announcement check, website docs, factory enrollment (`OPENCODE_FACTORY_MODEL=opencode/big-pickle`).

 // statNative returns the native file's size (bytes) and mtime (epoch ms), or zeros.
+//
+// A SQLite store in WAL mode (OpenCode's opencode.db, Cursor IDE's state.vscdb)
+// commits to <path>-wal and folds that into <path> only at a checkpoint, so the
+// main file alone can keep its size and mtime while a session changes. A -wal
+// sibling's size and mtime are folded in so such a change still reads as one;
+// paths without a -wal sibling keep the fingerprint they always had.
 func statNative(path string) (size, mtimeMs int64) {
 	info, err := os.Stat(path)
 	if err != nil {

+	if wal, err := os.Stat(path + "-wal"); err == nil {
+		size += wal.Size()
+		mtimeMs = max(mtimeMs, wal.ModTime().UnixMilli())
+	}
+	return size, mtimeMs
 }

+	// Without a -wal sibling the fingerprint is the file's own.
+	size, mtime := statNative(db)
+	if size != 4 || mtime != base.UnixMilli() {
+		t.Fatalf("statNative() = %d, %d; want the file's own size and mtime", size, mtime)
+	}
+
+	wal := db + "-wal"
+	if err := os.WriteFile(wal, []byte("first commit"), 0o644); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := os.Chtimes(wal, base.Add(time.Minute), base.Add(time.Minute)); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	withWAL, withWALMtime := statNative(db)
+	if withWAL == size && withWALMtime == mtime {
+		t.Fatal("a commit in the -wal file did not change the fingerprint")
+	}
+
+	// A later commit that leaves the WAL's size unchanged still changes it.
+	if err := os.Chtimes(wal, base.Add(2*time.Minute), base.Add(2*time.Minute)); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	laterSize, laterMtime := statNative(db)
+	if laterSize == withWAL && laterMtime == withWALMtime {
+		t.Error("a later -wal commit did not change the fingerprint")
+	}
+}

    34	// Provider implements spi.Provider for OpenCode.

    47	// Check verifies that the opencode binary resolves and reports a version.
    48	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
    49		cmdName, cmdArgs := parseOpenCodeCommand(customCommand)
    50		isCustom := customCommand != ""
    51		attempt := analytics.CheckAttempt{
    52			Provider:      providerID,
    53			CustomCommand: isCustom,
    54			CommandPath:   cmdName,
    55			VersionFlag:   versionFlag,
    56		}
    57	
    58		slog.Info("Check: verifying OpenCode installation", "command", cmdName, "customCommand", isCustom)
    59	
    60		resolvedPath, err := spi.LookPathForCheck(cmdName)
    61		if err != nil {
    62			errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckError(err)
    63			slog.Info("Check: binary lookup failed", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
    64			analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, err.Error(), "")
    65			return spi.CheckResult{
    66				Success:      false,
    67				ErrorType:    errorType,
    68				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, ""),
    69			}
    70		}
    71		attempt.ResolvedPath = resolvedPath
    72	
    73		// A custom command's arguments are part of how the user runs OpenCode (a
    74		// wrapper script may need them), so the probe keeps them.
    75		probeArgs := append(slices.Clone(cmdArgs), versionFlag)
    76		probeCommand := strings.Join(append([]string{cmdName}, probeArgs...), " ")
    77		if isCustom {
    78			probeCommand = customCommand + " " + versionFlag
    79		}
    80		cmd := exec.Command(resolvedPath, probeArgs...)
    81		var stdout bytes.Buffer
    82		var stderr bytes.Buffer
    83		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
    84		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
    85	
    86		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
    87			errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError(err)
    88			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
    89			slog.Info("Check: version probe failed",
    90				"resolved", resolvedPath,
    91				"errorType", errorType,
    92				"error", err,
    93				"stderr", stderrOutput)
    94			analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, err.Error(), stderrOutput)
    95			return spi.CheckResult{
    96				Success:      false,
    97				ErrorType:    errorType,
    98				Location:     resolvedPath,
    99				ErrorMessage: buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType, probeCommand, isCustom, stderrOutput),
   100			}
   101		}
   102	
   103		// Some wrappers print the version on stderr. A binary that prints nothing
   104		// still passes the check, reported as "unknown" so the result reads
   105		// unambiguously.
   106		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
   107		if version == "" {
   108			version = strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
   109		}
   110		if version == "" {
   111			version = "unknown"
   112		}
   113		slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "resolved", resolvedPath, "version", version)
   114		analytics.TrackCheckSuccess(attempt, version)
   115	
   116		return spi.CheckResult{
   117			Success:  true,
   118			Version:  version,
   119			Location: resolvedPath,
   120		}
   121	}

   123	func buildCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, command string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
   124		var b strings.Builder
   125	
   126		switch errorType {
   127		case spi.CheckErrorNotFound:
   128			b.WriteString("OpenCode could not be found.\n\n")
   129			if isCustom {
   130				b.WriteString("• Verify the path you supplied actually points to the `opencode` executable.\n")
   131				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Provided command: %s\n", command)
   132			} else {
   133				b.WriteString("• Install OpenCode (https://opencode.ai) and ensure `opencode` is on your PATH.\n")
   134				b.WriteString("• Or pass a custom command via `specstory check opencode -c \"path/to/opencode\"`.\n")
   135			}
   136		case spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied:
   137			b.WriteString("OpenCode exists but isn't executable.\n\n")
   138			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Fix permissions: `chmod +x %s`\n", command)
   139			b.WriteString("• Some package managers install the binary as root; run SpecStory with a path you can execute.\n")
   140		default:
   141			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "`%s` failed.\n\n", command)
   142			if stderr != "" {
   143				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Error output:\n%s\n\n", stderr)
   144			}
   145			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Try running `%s` directly in your terminal.\n", command)
   146			b.WriteString("• If you upgraded recently, reinstall OpenCode to refresh its installation.\n")
   147		}
   148	
   149		return b.String()
   150	}

   186	// GetAgentChatSessions returns every session started in the project directory.
   187	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
   188		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
   189		err := withDatabase(func(db *sql.DB) error {
   190			root, err := canonicalProjectPath(projectPath)
   191			if err != nil {
   192				return err
   193			}
   194			summaries, err := listSessionSummaries(db, root)
   195			if err != nil {
   196				return err
   197			}
   198			for i, summary := range summaries {
   199				snapshot, err := readSessionSnapshot(db, summary.ID)
   200				if err != nil {
   201					slog.Warn("GetAgentChatSessions: Failed to read OpenCode session, skipping",
   202						"sessionId", summary.ID, "error", err)
   203				} else if session := convertSnapshot(snapshot, root, debugRaw); session != nil {
   204					result = append(result, *session)
   205				}
   206				// Reported for every session, including skipped ones, so the
   207				// progress bar reaches its total.
   208				if progress != nil {
   209					progress(i+1, len(summaries))
   210				}
   211			}
   212			return nil
   213		})
   214		if errors.Is(err, errNoDatabase) {
   215			return nil, nil
   216		}
   217		return result, err
   218	}

   276	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {

   313	// ExecAgentAndWatch runs OpenCode interactively while watching the project's
   314	// sessions, and returns OpenCode's exit status only after the watcher has
   315	// delivered its final updates.
   316	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
   317		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Starting OpenCode",
   318			"projectPath", projectPath,
   319			"resumeSessionId", resumeSessionID,
   320			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
   321	
   322		root, err := canonicalProjectPath(projectPath)
   323		if err != nil {
   324			return err
   325		}
   326	
   327		// A reconstructed session is staged as an export file; OpenCode must load
   328		// it before `opencode -s <id>` can open it.
   329		if err := importStagedSession(customCommand, root, resumeSessionID); err != nil {
   330			return err
   331		}
   332	
   333		watcher, err := startWatcher(root, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
   334		if err != nil {
   335			// run still launches OpenCode; the sessions are recovered by a later sync.
   336			slog.Error("ExecAgentAndWatch: Failed to start OpenCode session watcher", "error", err)
   337		}
   338	
   339		execErr := executeOpenCode(customCommand, root, resumeSessionID)
   340	
   341		if watcher != nil {
   342			watcher.Stop()
   343		}
   344		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: OpenCode session finished", "error", execErr)
   345		return execErr
   346	}

   363		}
   364	
   365		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Watcher started, blocking until context cancelled")
   366		<-ctx.Done()
   367	
   368		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Context cancelled, stopping watcher")
   369		watcher.Stop()
   370		return ctx.Err()
   371	}
   372	
   373	// canonicalProjectPath returns the on-disk spelling of the project directory
   374	// (symlinks resolved, case corrected), which is how OpenCode records it.
   375	func canonicalProjectPath(projectPath string) (string, error) {
   376		if strings.TrimSpace(projectPath) == "" {
   377			cwd, err := os.Getwd()
   378			if err != nil {
   379				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current working directory: %w", err)
   380			}
   381			projectPath = cwd
   382		}
   383		canonical, err := spi.GetCanonicalPath(projectPath)
   384		if err != nil {
   385			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve project path %s: %w", projectPath, err)
   386		}
   387		return canonical, nil
   388	}
   389	
   390	// projectSessionSummaries lists the top-level sessions started in the project.
   391	func projectSessionSummaries(projectPath string) ([]sessionSummary, error) {
   392		var summaries []sessionSummary
   393		err := withDatabase(func(db *sql.DB) error {
   394			root, err := canonicalProjectPath(projectPath)
   395			if err != nil {
   396				return err
   397			}
   398			summaries, err = listSessionSummaries(db, root)
   399			return err
   400		})
   401		return summaries, err
   402	}
   403	
   404	// summaryMetadata builds listing metadata from a summary, or nil when the
   405	// session has no prompt yet. The slug is derived exactly as conversion derives
   406	// it so listings name sessions the way their markdown files are named.
   407	func summaryMetadata(summary sessionSummary) *spi.SessionMetadata {
   408		prompt := summaryPrompt(summary)
   409		if prompt == "" {
   410			return nil
   411		}
   412		slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(prompt)
   413		if slug == "" {
   414			slug = defaultSlug
   415		}
   416		name := strings.TrimSpace(summary.Title)
   417		if name == "" {
   418			name = spi.GenerateReadableName(prompt)
   419		}
   420		return &spi.SessionMetadata{
   421			SessionID: summary.ID,
   422			CreatedAt: formatMillis(summary.TimeCreated),
   423			Slug:      slug,
   424			Name:      name,
   425		}
   426	}
   427	
   428	// summaryPrompt names a session the way conversion does: its first user
   429	// prompt, else, for a session of shell commands only, its first command.
   430	func summaryPrompt(summary sessionSummary) string {
   431		if prompt := firstPromptText(summary.FirstUserData); prompt != "" {
   432			return prompt
   433		}
   434		if summary.FirstShellData == "" {
   435			return ""
   436		}
   437		var shell struct {
   438			Command string `json:"command"`
   439		}
   440		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(summary.FirstShellData), &shell); err != nil {
   441			slog.Debug("summaryPrompt: Unreadable OpenCode shell record", "error", err)
   442			return ""
   443		}
   444		return strings.TrimSpace(shell.Command)
   445	}
   446	
   447	// firstPromptText names a session from its first user record payload, the
   448	// same way conversion does.
   449	func firstPromptText(data string) string {
   450		if data == "" {
   451			return ""
   452		}
   453		var user nativeMessage
   454		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(data), &user); err != nil {
   455			slog.Debug("firstPromptText: Unreadable OpenCode user record", "error", err)
   456			return ""
   457		}
   458		return userPromptLabel(&user)
   459	}

   116	func getDataDir() (string, error) {

   131	func getDatabasePath() (string, error) {

   142		case filepath.IsAbs(override):

   149	// openDatabase opens OpenCode's database read-only. The file: scheme is
   150	// required for mode=ro to take effect; the busy timeout rides out the moments
   151	// when OpenCode's service holds a write lock.
   152	func openDatabase(dbPath string) (*sql.DB, error) {
   153		if _, err := os.Stat(dbPath); err != nil {
   154			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   155				return nil, errNoDatabase
   156			}
   157			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to access OpenCode database %s: %w", dbPath, err)
   158		}
   159		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?mode=ro&"+spi.BusyTimeoutPragma)
   160		if err != nil {
   161			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open OpenCode database %s: %w", dbPath, err)
   162		}
   163		// One connection is enough (SQLite serializes access anyway) and keeps a
   164		// long-running watch from accumulating file descriptors.
   165		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
   166		db.SetMaxIdleConns(1)
   167		return db, nil
   168	}

   170	// withDatabase opens the database, verifies it has the 2.x session schema,
   171	// runs fn, and closes it.
   172	func withDatabase(fn func(db *sql.DB) error) error {

   175			return err
   176		}

   178		if err != nil {
   179			return err
   180		}

   182			if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
   183				slog.Debug("Failed to close OpenCode database", "path", dbPath, "error", closeErr)
   184			}
   185		}()
   186		if err := verifySchema(db); err != nil {
   187			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dbPath, err)
   188		}
   189		return fn(db)
   190	}

   192	// verifySchema confirms the session tables exist. sql.Open is lazy, so this is
   193	// also the first query that proves the file is a readable SQLite database.
   194	func verifySchema(db *sql.DB) error {

   196		err := db.QueryRow(
   197			`SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name IN (?, ?)`,
   198			sessionTable, messageTable,
   199		).Scan(&count)
   200		if err != nil {
   201			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read OpenCode database schema: %w", err)
   202		}
   203		if count != 2 {
   204			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported OpenCode database: missing %s/%s tables (OpenCode 2.0.14 or newer is required)", sessionTable, messageTable)
   205		}
   206		return nil
   207	}
   208	
   209	// summaryQuery lists top-level sessions with the counters change detection
   210	// needs. Subagent sessions (parent_id set) belong to their parent's
   211	// conversation, so they are never listed on their own.
   212	//
   213	// The first-prompt subquery picks the first user record with text or an
   214	// attachment, the same record conversion names the session from; a record
   215	// with neither renders nothing. The first user shell command is read too, for
   216	// a session that has only those. json_valid guards json_extract, which would
   217	// otherwise abort the whole listing on one corrupt record.
   218	const summaryQuery = `
   219	SELECT s.id, s.directory, IFNULL(s.title, ''), s.time_created, s.time_updated,
   220	       (SELECT count(*) FROM session_message m WHERE m.session_id = s.id),
   221	       (SELECT IFNULL(max(m.time_updated), 0) FROM session_message m WHERE m.session_id = s.id),
   222	       IFNULL((SELECT m.data FROM session_message m
   223	               WHERE m.session_id = s.id AND m.type = 'user' AND json_valid(m.data)
   224	                 AND (trim(IFNULL(json_extract(m.data, '$.text'), ''), ' ' || char(9, 10, 13)) != ''
   225	                      OR IFNULL(json_array_length(m.data, '$.files'), 0) > 0
   226	                      OR IFNULL(json_array_length(m.data, '$.agents'), 0) > 0)
   227	               ORDER BY m.seq LIMIT 1), ''),
   228	       IFNULL((SELECT m.data FROM session_message m
   229	               WHERE m.session_id = s.id AND m.type = 'shell' AND json_valid(m.data)
   230	                 AND trim(IFNULL(json_extract(m.data, '$.command'), ''), ' ' || char(9, 10, 13)) != ''
   231	               ORDER BY m.seq LIMIT 1), '')
   232	FROM session_v2 s
   233	WHERE s.parent_id IS NULL`
   234	
   235	// listSessionSummaries returns the top-level sessions recorded for directory,
   236	// or every top-level session when directory is empty, oldest first.
   237	func listSessionSummaries(db *sql.DB, directory string) ([]sessionSummary, error) {
   238		query := summaryQuery
   239		var args []any
   240		if directory != "" {
   241			query += " AND s.directory = ?"
   242			args = append(args, directory)
   243		}
   244		query += " ORDER BY s.time_created, s.id"
   245	
   246		rows, err := db.Query(query, args...)
   247		if err != nil {
   248			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list OpenCode sessions: %w", err)
   249		}
   250		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }() // read-only cursor; close errors are not actionable
   251	
   252		var summaries []sessionSummary
   253		for rows.Next() {
   254			var s sessionSummary
   255			if err := rows.Scan(&s.ID, &s.Directory, &s.Title, &s.TimeCreated, &s.TimeUpdated,
   256				&s.MessageCount, &s.LastMessageUpdate, &s.FirstUserData, &s.FirstShellData); err != nil {
   257				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read OpenCode session row: %w", err)
   258			}
   259			summaries = append(summaries, s)
   260		}
   261		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
   262			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to list OpenCode sessions: %w", err)
   263		}
   264		return summaries, nil
   265	}
   266	
   267	// readSessionSnapshot reads one session and all of its messages inside a
   268	// single read transaction. It returns nil, nil when the session does not exist.
   269	func readSessionSnapshot(db *sql.DB, sessionID string) (*sessionSnapshot, error) {
   270		tx, err := db.BeginTx(context.Background(), &sql.TxOptions{ReadOnly: true})
   271		if err != nil {
   272			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to begin OpenCode read transaction: %w", err)
   273		}
   274		// A read-only transaction has nothing to commit; rollback just releases it.
   275		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
   276	
   277		sessionRows, err := queryRowMaps(tx, `SELECT * FROM session_v2 WHERE id = ?`, nil, sessionID)
   278		if err != nil {
   279			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read OpenCode session %s: %w", sessionID, err)
   280		}
   281		if len(sessionRows) == 0 {
   282			return nil, nil
   283		}
   284	
   285		// data is the only JSON payload column in session_message; embedding it
   286		// as raw JSON keeps the export readable instead of double-encoded.
   287		messageRows, err := queryRowMaps(tx,
   288			`SELECT * FROM session_message WHERE session_id = ? ORDER BY seq`,
   289			map[string]bool{"data": true}, sessionID)
   290		if err != nil {
   291			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read OpenCode messages for %s: %w", sessionID, err)
   292		}
   293	
   294		snapshot := &sessionSnapshot{Session: newSessionRecord(sessionRows[0])}
   295		for _, row := range messageRows {
   296			snapshot.Messages = append(snapshot.Messages, newMessageRecord(row))
   297		}
   298		return snapshot, nil
   299	}
   300	
   301	// queryRowMaps runs a query and returns each row as a column-name map, so
   302	// every column (including ones added by a later OpenCode) is carried through.
   303	// Columns named in jsonColumns are embedded as json.RawMessage when they hold
   304	// valid JSON.
   305	func queryRowMaps(tx *sql.Tx, query string, jsonColumns map[string]bool, args ...any) ([]map[string]any, error) {
   306		rows, err := tx.Query(query, args...)
   307		if err != nil {
   308			return nil, err
   309		}
   310		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }() // read-only cursor; close errors are not actionable
   311	
   312		columns, err := rows.Columns()
   313		if err != nil {
   314			return nil, err
   315		}
   316	
   317		var result []map[string]any
   318		for rows.Next() {
   319			values := make([]any, len(columns))
   320			pointers := make([]any, len(columns))
   321			for i := range values {
   322				pointers[i] = &values[i]
   323			}
   324			if err := rows.Scan(pointers...); err != nil {
   325				return nil, err
   326			}
   327			row := make(map[string]any, len(columns))
   328			for i, column := range columns {
   329				value := values[i]
   330				// The driver returns TEXT as string but BLOB as []byte; either way
   331				// a string is what the JSON export should show.
   332				if b, ok := value.([]byte); ok {
   333					value = string(b)
   334				}
   335				if s, ok := value.(string); ok && jsonColumns[column] && json.Valid([]byte(s)) {
   336					value = json.RawMessage(s)
   337				}
   338				row[column] = value
   339			}
   340			result = append(result, row)
   341		}
   342		return result, rows.Err()
   343	}
   344	
   345	func newSessionRecord(row map[string]any) sessionRecord {
   346		return sessionRecord{
   347			ID:          columnString(row, "id"),
   348			ParentID:    columnString(row, "parent_id"),
   349			Directory:   columnString(row, "directory"),
   350			Title:       columnString(row, "title"),
   351			Version:     columnString(row, "version"),
   352			TimeCreated: columnInt(row, "time_created"),
   353			TimeUpdated: columnInt(row, "time_updated"),
   354			Row:         row,
   355		}
   356	}
   357	
   358	func newMessageRecord(row map[string]any) messageRecord {
   359		record := messageRecord{
   360			ID:          columnString(row, "id"),
   361			Type:        columnString(row, "type"),
   362			Seq:         columnInt(row, "seq"),
   363			TimeCreated: columnInt(row, "time_created"),
   364			TimeUpdated: columnInt(row, "time_updated"),
   365			Row:         row,
   366		}
   367		switch data := row["data"].(type) {
   368		case json.RawMessage:
   369			record.Data = data
   370		case string:
   371			// Not valid JSON (queryRowMaps only embeds valid payloads); keep the
   372			// text so the parser can report the corrupt record.
   373			record.Data = json.RawMessage(data)
   374		}
   375		return record
   376	}
   377	
   378	func columnString(row map[string]any, column string) string {
   379		switch v := row[column].(type) {
   380		case string:
   381			return v
   382		case json.RawMessage:
   383			return string(v)
   384		}
   385		return ""
   386	}
   387	
   388	func columnInt(row map[string]any, column string) int64 {
   389		switch v := row[column].(type) {
   390		case int64:
   391			return v
   392		case float64:
   393			return int64(v)
   394		}
   395		return 0
   396	}

    84		Output    float64 `json:"output"`
    85		Reasoning float64 `json:"reasoning"`
    86		Cache     struct {
    87			Read  float64 `json:"read"`
    88			Write float64 `json:"write"`
    89		} `json:"cache"`
    90	}
    91	
    92	type recordTime struct {
    93		Created   int64 `json:"created"`
    94		Completed int64 `json:"completed,omitempty"`
    95	}
    96	
    97	// fileAttachment is a file the user attached to a prompt. data (the base64
    98	// body) is deliberately not decoded.

   100		Name        string `json:"name"`

   114	// toolContent is one item of a tool result: text, or a file reference.

   123	// toolState carries a call's arguments and, once it finishes, its result.
   124	// Input is an object except while streaming, when it is the partial argument

   127		Status   string           `json:"status"`

   134	// contentPart is one element of an assistant step's content array.

   143	
   144	// nativeMessage is the union of every session_message payload. Fields are
   145	// shared across record types where OpenCode uses the same name (text, agent,
   146	// model, status).
   147	type nativeMessage struct {
   148		Time     recordTime     `json:"time"`
   149		Metadata map[string]any `json:"metadata"`
   150	
   151		// user, synthetic, system, skill
   152		Text   string            `json:"text"`
   153		Files  []fileAttachment  `json:"files"`
   154		Agents []agentAttachment `json:"agents"`
   155	
   156		// assistant
   157		Agent   string           `json:"agent"`
   158		Model   *modelRef        `json:"model"`
   159		Content []contentPart    `json:"content"`
   160		Finish  string           `json:"finish"`
   161		Error   *structuredError `json:"error"`
   162		Tokens  *tokenUsage      `json:"tokens"`
   163	
   164		// shell (status is shared with compaction)
   165		Command string          `json:"command"`
   166		Status  string          `json:"status"`
   167		Exit    json.RawMessage `json:"exit"`
   168		Output  *shellOutput    `json:"output"`
   169	
   170		// compaction
   171		Reason  string `json:"reason"`
   172		Summary string `json:"summary"`
   173	}
   174	
   175	// rawRecord is one row of the native transcript as carried in RawData and the
   176	// debug export: the table it came from and every column it holds.
   177	type rawRecord struct {
   178		Table string         `json:"table"`
   179		Row   map[string]any `json:"row"`
   180	}
   181	
   182	// convertSnapshot turns a session snapshot into the provider-agnostic session.
   183	// It returns nil when the session has neither a user prompt nor a user shell
   184	// command yet (OpenCode creates the session row before the first message
   185	// arrives).
   186	func convertSnapshot(snapshot *sessionSnapshot, projectPath string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
   187		if snapshot == nil {
   188			return nil
   189		}
   190		sessionData, firstPrompt := buildSessionData(snapshot, projectPath)
   191		if firstPrompt == "" {
   192			slog.Debug("convertSnapshot: Session has no user prompt yet", "sessionId", snapshot.Session.ID)
   193			return nil
   194		}
   195	
   196		if debugRaw {
   197			if err := writeDebugRawFiles(snapshot); err != nil {
   198				slog.Warn("convertSnapshot: Failed to write debug files",
   199					"sessionId", snapshot.Session.ID,
   200					"path", spi.GetDebugDir(snapshot.Session.ID),
   201					"error", err)
   202			}
   203		}
   204	
   205		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
   206			SessionID:   snapshot.Session.ID,
   207			CreatedAt:   sessionData.CreatedAt,
   208			Slug:        sessionData.Slug,
   209			SessionData: sessionData,
   210			RawData:     buildRawData(snapshot),
   211		}
   212	}
   213	
   214	// buildSessionData converts the snapshot's records into SessionData and
   215	// returns the first user prompt, which names the session.
   216	func buildSessionData(snapshot *sessionSnapshot, projectPath string) (*schema.SessionData, string) {
   217		session := snapshot.Session
   218		workspaceRoot := resolveWorkspaceRoot(session.Directory, projectPath)
   219	
   220		version := strings.TrimSpace(session.Version)
   221		if version == "" {
   222			version = "unknown"
   223		}
   224	
   225		builder := &exchangeBuilder{sessionID: session.ID, workspaceRoot: workspaceRoot}
   226		for i := range snapshot.Messages {
   227			builder.addRecord(&snapshot.Messages[i])
   228		}
   229		builder.flush()
   230		if builder.firstPrompt == "" {
   231			// A session of user shell commands only is named by its first one.
   232			builder.firstPrompt = builder.firstShell
   233		}
   234	
   235		slug := defaultSlug
   236		if builder.firstPrompt != "" {
   237			if generated := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(builder.firstPrompt); generated != "" {
   238				slug = generated
   239			}
   240		}
   241	
   242		return &schema.SessionData{
   243			SchemaVersion: schema.CurrentSchemaVersion,
   244			Provider: schema.ProviderInfo{
   245				ID:      providerID,
   246				Name:    providerName,
   247				Version: version,
   248			},
   249			SessionID:     session.ID,
   250			CreatedAt:     formatMillis(session.TimeCreated),
   251			UpdatedAt:     formatMillis(session.TimeUpdated),
   252			Slug:          slug,
   253			WorkspaceRoot: workspaceRoot,
   254			Exchanges:     builder.exchanges,
   255		}, builder.firstPrompt
   256	}
   257	
   258	// resolveWorkspaceRoot prefers the directory OpenCode recorded, then the
   259	// caller's project, then the process working directory as a last resort so
   260	// the workspace root is never empty (path normalization depends on it).
   261	func resolveWorkspaceRoot(recorded, projectPath string) string {
   262		if strings.TrimSpace(recorded) != "" {
   263			return recorded
   264		}
   265		if strings.TrimSpace(projectPath) != "" {
   266			return projectPath
   267		}
   268		if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
   269			return cwd
   270		}
   271		return "."
   272	}
   273	
   274	// exchangeBuilder groups records into exchanges: each user prompt or user
   275	// shell command opens one, and everything the agent does until the next
   276	// opens is appended to it.
   277	type exchangeBuilder struct {
   278		sessionID     string
   279		workspaceRoot string
   280		exchanges     []schema.Exchange
   281		current       *schema.Exchange
   282		firstPrompt   string
   283		firstShell    string
   284	}
   285	
   286	func (b *exchangeBuilder) addRecord(record *messageRecord) {
   287		var msg nativeMessage
   288		if err := json.Unmarshal(record.Data, &msg); err != nil {
   289			slog.Warn("Skipping corrupted OpenCode message record",
   290				"sessionId", b.sessionID,
   291				"messageId", record.ID,
   292				"seq", record.Seq,
   293				"error", err)
   294			return
   295		}
   296		created := msg.Time.Created
   297		if created == 0 {
   298			created = record.TimeCreated
   299		}
   300		timestamp := formatMillis(created)
   301	
   302		switch record.Type {
   303		case recordUser:
   304			b.addUser(record.ID, timestamp, &msg)
   305		case recordShell:
   306			b.addShell(record.ID, timestamp, &msg)
   307		case recordAssistant:
   308			b.addAssistant(record.ID, timestamp, &msg)
   309		case recordCompaction:
   310			b.addCompaction(record.ID, timestamp, &msg)
   311		case recordSynthetic, recordSystem, recordSkill:
   312			// Text OpenCode injects for the model (shell output echoes, Plan-mode
   313			// reminders, skill bodies), not something the user or agent said.
   314			slog.Debug("Skipping OpenCode scaffolding record", "sessionId", b.sessionID, "type", record.Type, "seq", record.Seq)
   315		case recordIdle, recordAgentSwitched, recordModelSwitched, recordLocationSwitched:
   316			// Lifecycle and configuration markers with no conversational content;
   317			// the agent and model they announce are recorded on each assistant step.
   318			slog.Debug("Skipping OpenCode lifecycle record", "sessionId", b.sessionID, "type", record.Type, "seq", record.Seq)
   319		default:
   320			slog.Debug("Skipping unknown OpenCode record type", "sessionId", b.sessionID, "type", record.Type, "seq", record.Seq)
   321		}
   322	}
   323	
   324	// startExchange closes the current exchange and opens a new one.
   325	func (b *exchangeBuilder) startExchange(id, timestamp string) {
   326		b.flush()
   327		b.current = &schema.Exchange{ExchangeID: id, StartTime: timestamp}
   328	}
   329	
   330	// appendMessage adds a message to the current exchange, opening one when the
   331	// agent speaks before any prompt (a compaction or an error at the very start).
   332	func (b *exchangeBuilder) appendMessage(id string, message schema.Message) {
   333		if b.current == nil {
   334			b.startExchange(id, message.Timestamp)
   335		}
   336		b.current.Messages = append(b.current.Messages, message)
   337		if message.Timestamp != "" {
   338			b.current.EndTime = message.Timestamp
   339		}
   340	}
   341	
   342	func (b *exchangeBuilder) flush() {
   343		if b.current != nil && len(b.current.Messages) > 0 {
   344			b.exchanges = append(b.exchanges, *b.current)
   345		}
   346		b.current = nil
   347	}
   348	
   349	func (b *exchangeBuilder) addUser(id, timestamp string, msg *nativeMessage) {
   350		var parts []schema.ContentPart
   351		if strings.TrimSpace(msg.Text) != "" {
   352			parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: msg.Text})
   353		}
   354		if attachments := formatAttachments(msg.Files, msg.Agents); attachments != "" {
   355			parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: attachments})
   356		}
   357		if len(parts) == 0 {
   358			slog.Debug("Skipping empty OpenCode user record", "sessionId", b.sessionID, "messageId", id)
   359			return
   360		}
   361		if b.firstPrompt == "" {
   362			b.firstPrompt = userPromptLabel(msg)
   363		}
   364		b.startExchange(id, timestamp)
   365		b.appendMessage(id, schema.Message{
   366			ID:        id,
   367			Timestamp: timestamp,
   368			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
   369			Content:   parts,
   370		})
   371	}
   372	
   373	// userPromptLabel names a user record for slugs and listings: its text, or,
   374	// for a prompt that carries only attachments, the attachments themselves.
   375	// Listing and conversion both use it so a session is named the same way by
   376	// each.
   377	func userPromptLabel(msg *nativeMessage) string {
   378		if text := strings.TrimSpace(msg.Text); text != "" {
   379			return text
   380		}
   381		var names []string
   382		for _, file := range msg.Files {
   383			if name := strings.TrimSpace(file.Name); name != "" {
   384				names = append(names, name)
   385			}
   386		}
   387		for _, agent := range msg.Agents {
   388			if name := strings.TrimSpace(agent.Name); name != "" {
   389				names = append(names, "@"+name)
   390			}
   391		}
   392		if len(names) == 0 && len(msg.Files) > 0 {
   393			names = append(names, "attachment")
   394		}
   395		return strings.Join(names, " ")
   396	}
   397	
   398	// formatAttachments lists the files and agents attached to a prompt. File
   399	// bodies are base64 payloads and are not reproduced.
   400	func formatAttachments(files []fileAttachment, agents []agentAttachment) string {
   401		var lines []string
   402		for _, file := range files {
   403			name := strings.TrimSpace(file.Name)
   404			if name == "" {
   405				name = "(unnamed)"
   406			}
   407			line := "- Attached file: " + inlineCode(name)
   408			if file.Mime != "" {
   409				line += fmt.Sprintf(" (%s)", file.Mime)
   410			}
   411			lines = append(lines, line)
   412		}
   413		for _, agent := range agents {
   414			if strings.TrimSpace(agent.Name) != "" {
   415				lines = append(lines, "- Mentioned agent: "+inlineCode("@"+agent.Name))
   416			}
   417		}
   418		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
   419	}
   420	
   421	// addShell renders a user's `!command` as a labeled user message so it reads
   422	// as historical activity rather than a new instruction.
   423	func (b *exchangeBuilder) addShell(id, timestamp string, msg *nativeMessage) {
   424		if strings.TrimSpace(msg.Command) == "" {
   425			return
   426		}
   427		if b.firstShell == "" {
   428			b.firstShell = strings.TrimSpace(msg.Command)
   429		}
   430		parts := []schema.ContentPart{{
   431			Type: schema.ContentTypeText,
   432			Text: "User ran a shell command:\n\n" + spi.CodeFence("bash", msg.Command),
   433		}}
   434		if result := formatUserShellResult(msg); result != "" {
   435			parts = append(parts, schema.ContentPart{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: result})
   436		}
   437		b.startExchange(id, timestamp)
   438		b.appendMessage(id, schema.Message{
   439			ID:        id,
   440			Timestamp: timestamp,
   441			Role:      schema.RoleUser,
   442			Content:   parts,
   443		})
   444	}
   445	
   446	func formatUserShellResult(msg *nativeMessage) string {
   447		var sections []string
   448		if msg.Output != nil {
   449			if output := strings.TrimRight(sanitizeShellOutput(msg.Output.Output), "\n"); output != "" {
   450				sections = append(sections, "Output:\n\n"+spi.CodeFence("text", spi.CapRunes(output, maxResultRunes)))
   451			}
   452			if msg.Output.Truncated {
   453				sections = append(sections, "[Output truncated by OpenCode]")
   454			}
   455		}
   456		if exit := exitCodeText(msg.Exit); exit != "" {
   457			sections = append(sections, "Exit code: "+exit)
   458		}
   459		switch msg.Status {
   460		case shellTimeout:
   461			sections = append(sections, "Timed out.")
   462		case shellKilled:
   463			sections = append(sections, "Killed.")
   464		case shellRunning:
   465			sections = append(sections, "Still running.")
   466		}
   467		return strings.Join(sections, "\n\n")
   468	}
   469	
   470	// exitCodeText renders a shell exit status, which OpenCode records as a number
   471	// or, for a signal, as a string such as "Infinity".
   472	func exitCodeText(raw json.RawMessage) string {
   473		if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
   474			return ""
   475		}
   476		var number json.Number
   477		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &number); err == nil {
   478			return number.String()
   479		}
   480		var text string
   481		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &text); err == nil {
   482			return text
   483		}
   484		return ""
   485	}
   486	
   487	func (b *exchangeBuilder) addAssistant(id, timestamp string, msg *nativeMessage) {
   488		model := modelID(msg)
   489	
   490		var produced []schema.Message
   491		// Text parts carry no time of their own; they take the latest time seen
   492		// earlier in the step so timestamps never run backwards within it.
   493		partTimestamp := timestamp
   494		for i := range msg.Content {
   495			part := &msg.Content[i]
   496			if part.Time != nil && part.Time.Created != 0 {
   497				if own := formatMillis(part.Time.Created); own > partTimestamp {
   498					partTimestamp = own
   499				}
   500			}
   501			partID := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", id, i)
   502	
   503			switch part.Type {
   504			case partText:
   505				if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) == "" {
   506					// OpenCode stores whitespace-only text between tool calls.
   507					continue
   508				}
   509				produced = append(produced, schema.Message{
   510					ID: partID, Timestamp: partTimestamp, Role: schema.RoleAgent, Model: model,
   511					Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: part.Text}},
   512				})
   513			case partReasoning:
   514				if strings.TrimSpace(part.Text) == "" {
   515					// Encrypted reasoning has only an opaque blob and no text.
   516					continue
   517				}
   518				produced = append(produced, schema.Message{
   519					ID: partID, Timestamp: partTimestamp, Role: schema.RoleAgent, Model: model,
   520					Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: part.Text}},
   521				})
   522			case partTool:
   523				produced = append(produced, b.toolMessage(partID, partTimestamp, model, part))
   524			default:
   525				slog.Debug("Skipping unknown OpenCode assistant part", "sessionId", b.sessionID, "messageId", id, "partType", part.Type)
   526			}
   527		}
   528	
   529		if msg.Error != nil && strings.TrimSpace(msg.Error.Message) != "" {
   530			// The failure ends the step, so it follows any part already shown.
   531			produced = append(produced, schema.Message{
   532				ID: id + ":error", Timestamp: partTimestamp, Role: schema.RoleAgent, Model: model,
   533				Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "[error] " + msg.Error.Message}},
   534			})
   535		}
   536	
   537		if len(produced) == 0 {
   538			return
   539		}
   540		// Usage belongs to the whole step, so it is recorded once, on the step's
   541		// last message, rather than repeated on every part.
   542		produced[len(produced)-1].Usage = mapUsage(msg.Tokens)
   543		for _, message := range produced {
   544			b.appendMessage(id, message)
   545		}
   546	}
   547	
   548	// toolMessage converts a tool part into an agent message carrying the call,
   549	// its result, and pre-rendered markdown.
   550	func (b *exchangeBuilder) toolMessage(id, timestamp, model string, part *contentPart) schema.Message {
   551		input, output := toolInputOutput(part.State)
   552		tool := &schema.ToolInfo{
   553			Name:   part.Name,
   554			Type:   toolType(part.Name),
   555			UseID:  part.ID,
   556			Input:  input,
   557			Output: output,
   558		}
   559		formatted := formatToolAsMarkdown(tool)
   560		tool.FormattedMarkdown = &formatted
   561	
   562		return schema.Message{
   563			ID:        id,
   564			Timestamp: timestamp,
   565			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
   566			Model:     model,
   567			Tool:      tool,
   568			PathHints: toolPathHints(part.Name, input, b.workspaceRoot),
   569		}
   570	}
   571	
   572	// toolInputOutput decodes a tool state into the ToolInfo input and output
   573	// maps. The output map is the provider's own shape, read back by the
   574	// renderers: status, joined text content, file references, error, metadata.
   575	func toolInputOutput(state *toolState) (map[string]any, map[string]any) {
   576		if state == nil {
   577			return nil, nil
   578		}
   579	
   580		var input map[string]any
   581		if len(state.Input) > 0 {
   582			if err := json.Unmarshal(state.Input, &input); err != nil {
   583				// A streaming call's input is the partial argument string.
   584				var partial string
   585				if json.Unmarshal(state.Input, &partial) == nil && partial != "" {
   586					input = map[string]any{"partialInput": partial}
   587				}
   588			}
   589		}
   590	
   591		output := map[string]any{"status": state.Status}
   592		var texts []string
   593		var files []string
   594		for _, item := range state.Content {
   595			switch item.Type {
   596			case toolContentText:
   597				texts = append(texts, item.Text)
   598			case toolContentFile:
   599				files = append(files, describeFileContent(item))
   600			}
   601		}
   602		if len(texts) > 0 {
   603			output["texts"] = texts
   604		}
   605		if len(files) > 0 {
   606			output["files"] = files
   607		}
   608		if state.Error != nil && strings.TrimSpace(state.Error.Message) != "" {
   609			output["error"] = state.Error.Message
   610		}
   611		if len(state.Metadata) > 0 {
   612			output["metadata"] = state.Metadata
   613		}
   614		return input, output
   615	}
   616	
   617	func describeFileContent(item toolContent) string {
   618		label := item.Name
   619		if label == "" {
   620			label = item.URI
   621		}
   622		if item.Mime != "" {
   623			return fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s)", label, item.Mime)
   624		}
   625		return label
   626	}
   627	
   628	// addCompaction renders a finished compaction's summary, which OpenCode shows
   629	// in place of the compacted history, and a failed compaction's error.
   630	func (b *exchangeBuilder) addCompaction(id, timestamp string, msg *nativeMessage) {
   631		var text string
   632		switch msg.Status {
   633		case compactionCompleted:
   634			if strings.TrimSpace(msg.Summary) == "" {
   635				return
   636			}
   637			text = fmt.Sprintf("Conversation compacted (%s). Summary:\n\n%s", msg.Reason, msg.Summary)
   638		case compactionFailed:
   639			if msg.Error == nil || strings.TrimSpace(msg.Error.Message) == "" {
   640				return
   641			}
   642			text = "[error] Conversation compaction failed: " + msg.Error.Message
   643		default:
   644			// A running compaction is rewritten in place once it finishes.
   645			return
   646		}
   647		model := modelID(msg)
   648		b.appendMessage(id, schema.Message{
   649			ID:        id,
   650			Timestamp: timestamp,
   651			Role:      schema.RoleAgent,
   652			Model:     model,
   653			Content:   []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: text}},
   654			Usage:     mapUsage(msg.Tokens),
   655		})
   656	}
   657	
   658	// modelID returns the id of the model that produced a record, or "" when the
   659	// record names none.
   660	func modelID(msg *nativeMessage) string {
   661		if msg.Model == nil {
   662			return ""
   663		}
   664		return msg.Model.ID
   665	}
   666	
   667	// mapUsage keeps OpenCode's distinct token kinds: input excludes cache reads,
   668	// and reasoning is counted separately from output.
   669	func mapUsage(tokens *tokenUsage) *schema.Usage {
   670		if tokens == nil {
   671			return nil
   672		}
   673		usage := &schema.Usage{
   674			InputTokens:              int(tokens.Input),
   675			OutputTokens:             int(tokens.Output),
   676			ReasoningOutputTokens:    int(tokens.Reasoning),
   677			CacheReadInputTokens:     int(tokens.Cache.Read),
   678			CacheCreationInputTokens: int(tokens.Cache.Write),
   679		}
   680		if *usage == (schema.Usage{}) {
   681			return nil
   682		}
   683		return usage
   684	}
   685	
   686	// formatMillis renders an OpenCode Unix-millisecond timestamp as RFC 3339.
   687	func formatMillis(ms int64) string {
   688		if ms <= 0 {
   689			return ""
   690		}
   691		return time.UnixMilli(ms).UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z")
   692	}
   693	
   694	// buildRawData serializes the snapshot as JSON lines: the session row, then
   695	// every message row in sequence order.
   696	func buildRawData(snapshot *sessionSnapshot) string {
   697		var b strings.Builder
   698		encoder := json.NewEncoder(&b)
   699		// Keep <, > and & as written (shell commands, markup) instead of the
   700		// \u0026-style escapes json.Marshal applies for HTML embedding.
   701		encoder.SetEscapeHTML(false)
   702		for _, record := range rawRecords(snapshot) {
   703			// Encode writes the record followed by a newline, giving JSON lines.
   704			if err := encoder.Encode(record); err != nil {
   705				slog.Warn("buildRawData: Failed to encode OpenCode record", "sessionId", snapshot.Session.ID, "table", record.Table, "error", err)
   706			}
   707		}
   708		return b.String()
   709	}
   710	
   711	func rawRecords(snapshot *sessionSnapshot) []rawRecord {
   712		records := make([]rawRecord, 0, len(snapshot.Messages)+1)
   713		records = append(records, rawRecord{Table: sessionTable, Row: snapshot.Session.Row})
   714		for _, message := range snapshot.Messages {
   715			records = append(records, rawRecord{Table: messageTable, Row: message.Row})
   716		}
   717		return records
   718	}
   719	
   720	// writeDebugRawFiles exports the snapshot as numbered, pretty-printed records:
   721	// 1.json is the session row, followed by one file per message in sequence
   722	// order, each with every column OpenCode stored.
   723	func writeDebugRawFiles(snapshot *sessionSnapshot) error {
   724		return spi.WriteDebugRecords(spi.GetDebugDir(snapshot.Session.ID), rawRecords(snapshot))
   725	}

   121	// inlineCode wraps text in a backtick span long enough to contain any
   122	// backticks inside it, keeping it on one line.
   123	func inlineCode(text string) string {

   126		for strings.Contains(text, fence) {

   128		}
   129		if strings.HasPrefix(text, "`") || strings.HasSuffix(text, "`") {
   130			return fence + " " + text + " " + fence
   131		}
   132		return fence + text + fence
   133	}

   298	// formatToolResult renders a call's outcome. A failure takes priority over

   300	func formatToolResult(name string, input, output map[string]any) string {

   303		}
   304		texts := outputTexts(output)
   305		var sections []string

   310				sections = append(sections, resultBlock("text", joined))
   311			}

   314	
   315		switch spi.StringValue(output, "status") {
   316		case statusRunning, statusStreaming:
   317			return "_Still running._"
   318		}

   320		switch name {
   321		case toolRead:
   322			sections = append(sections, formatReadResult(spi.StringValue(input, "path"), texts))
   323		case toolWrite, toolEdit:
   324			sections = append(sections, formatAcknowledgement(texts))
   325		case toolShell:
   326			sections = append(sections, formatShellResult(output, texts))

   342			// Code Mode returns whatever the script returned; a returned object

   366	func outputTexts(output map[string]any) []string {
   367		texts, _ := output["texts"].([]string)
   368		return texts
   369	}
   370	
   371	// resultBlock renders a result in a fence tagged lang, capped with a visible
   372	// marker. Empty results render nothing.
   373	func resultBlock(lang, text string) string {
   374		text = strings.Trim(text, "\n")
   375		if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
   376			return ""
   377		}
   378		return "Result:\n\n" + spi.CodeFence(lang, spi.CapRunes(text, maxResultRunes))
   379	}
   380	
   381	// formatReadResult shows what OpenCode returned with its header ("Read file
   382	// <path>, lines a-b" or "Read directory <path>, entries a-b") as a caption: a
   383	// file in a fence tagged by its extension, a directory listing as text.
   384	func formatReadResult(path string, texts []string) string {
   385		text := strings.Trim(strings.Join(texts, "\n"), "\n")
   386		if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
   387			return ""
   388		}
   389		header, rest, found := strings.Cut(text, "\n")
   390		var lang string
   391		switch {
   392		case strings.HasPrefix(header, "Read file "):
   393			lang = spi.LanguageFromPath(path)
   394		case strings.HasPrefix(header, "Read directory "):
   395			lang = "text"
   396		default:
   397			return resultBlock(spi.LanguageFromPath(path), text)
   398		}
   399		if !found || strings.TrimSpace(rest) == "" {
   400			return header
   401		}
   402		return header + "\n\n" + spi.CodeFence(lang, spi.CapRunes(rest, maxResultRunes))
   403	}
   404	
   405	// formatAcknowledgement renders a one-line confirmation inline and anything
   406	// longer in a fence.
   407	func formatAcknowledgement(texts []string) string {
   408		text := strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(texts, "\n"))
   409		if text == "" {
   410			return ""
   411		}
   412		if !strings.Contains(text, "\n") {
   413			return "Result: " + text
   414		}
   415		return resultBlock("text", text)
   416	}
   417	
   418	// formatShellResult renders shell output with terminal control bytes removed,
   419	// then the exit code from metadata.
   420	func formatShellResult(output map[string]any, texts []string) string {
   421		metadata, _ := output["metadata"].(map[string]any)
   422		exit := spi.StringValue(metadata, "exit")
   423	
   424		var kept []string
   425		for _, text := range texts {
   426			if exit != "" && exitNoticePattern.MatchString(strings.TrimSpace(text)) {
   427				continue
   428			}
   429			kept = append(kept, text)
   430		}
   431	
   432		var sections []string
   433		if block := resultBlock("text", sanitizeShellOutput(strings.Join(kept, "\n"))); block != "" {
   434			sections = append(sections, block)
   435		}
   436		if truncated, ok := metadata["truncated"].(bool); ok && truncated {
   437			sections = append(sections, "[Output truncated by OpenCode]")
   438		}
   439		if exit != "" {
   440			sections = append(sections, "Exit code: "+exit)
   441		}
   442		return strings.Join(sections, "\n\n")
   443	}
   444	
   445	// subagentTagPattern matches the wrapper OpenCode puts around a subagent's
   446	// answer: <subagent sessionID="..." state="...">.
   447	var subagentTagPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)^<subagent\s+sessionID="([^"]*)"\s+state="([^"]*)">\n?(.*?)\n?</subagent>$`)
   448	
   449	func formatSubagentResult(texts []string) string {
   450		text := strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(texts, "\n"))
   451		if text == "" {
   452			return ""
   453		}
   454		match := subagentTagPattern.FindStringSubmatch(text)
   455		if match == nil {
   456			return resultBlock("markdown", text)
   457		}
   458		lines := []string{fmt.Sprintf("Subagent session: %s (%s)", inlineCode(match[1]), match[2])}
   459		if block := resultBlock("markdown", match[3]); block != "" {
   460			lines = append(lines, block)
   461		}
   462		return strings.Join(lines, "\n\n")
   463	}
   464	
   465	// unwrapTag strips an XML-style wrapper OpenCode adds for the model, such as
   466	// <skill_content name="...">...</skill_content>, leaving the content itself.
   467	func unwrapTag(text, tag string) string {
   468		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(text)
   469		if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<"+tag) || !strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "</"+tag+">") {
   470			return text
   471		}
   472		_, inner, found := strings.Cut(trimmed, ">")
   473		if !found {
   474			return text
   475		}
   476		return strings.TrimSuffix(inner, "</"+tag+">")
   477	}
   478	
   479	// formatQuestionAnswers renders the user's answers from metadata.answers (one
   480	// list of chosen labels per question). The text result restates them for the
   481	// model, so it is shown only when no answers were recorded.
   482	func formatQuestionAnswers(output map[string]any, texts []string) string {
   483		metadata, _ := output["metadata"].(map[string]any)
   484		answers, _ := metadata["answers"].([]any)
   485		var chosen []string
   486		for _, entry := range answers {
   487			labels, _ := entry.([]any)
   488			var picked []string
   489			for _, label := range labels {
   490				if text, ok := label.(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(text) != "" {
   491					picked = append(picked, text)
   492				}
   493			}
   494			if len(picked) > 0 {
   495				chosen = append(chosen, strings.Join(picked, ", "))
   496			}
   497		}
   498		if len(chosen) == 0 {
   499			return resultBlock("text", strings.Join(texts, "\n"))
   500		}
   501		if len(chosen) == 1 {
   502			return "Answer: " + chosen[0]
   503		}
   504		lines := []string{"Answers:"}
   505		for _, answer := range chosen {
   506			lines = append(lines, "- "+answer)
   507		}
   508		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
   509	}
   510	
   511	// formatInnerToolCalls lists the catalog calls an execute run made, from
   512	// metadata.toolCalls.
   513	func formatInnerToolCalls(output map[string]any) string {
   514		metadata, _ := output["metadata"].(map[string]any)
   515		calls, _ := metadata["toolCalls"].([]any)
   516		var lines []string
   517		for _, entry := range calls {
   518			call, ok := entry.(map[string]any)
   519			if !ok {
   520				continue
   521			}
   522			name := spi.StringValue(call, "tool")
   523			if name == "" {
   524				continue
   525			}
   526			line := "- " + inlineCode(name)
   527			if status := spi.StringValue(call, "status"); status != "" {
   528				line += " — " + status
   529			}
   530			lines = append(lines, line)
   531		}
   532		if len(lines) == 0 {
   533			return ""
   534		}
   535		return "Tool calls:\n\n" + strings.Join(lines, "\n")
   536	}
   537	
   538	func joinNonEmpty(sections []string) string {
   539		var kept []string
   540		for _, section := range sections {
   541			if strings.TrimSpace(section) != "" {
   542				kept = append(kept, section)
   543			}
   544		}
   545		return strings.Join(kept, "\n\n")
   546	}
   547	
   548	// sanitizeShellOutput strips ANSI escape sequences and the remaining control
   549	// bytes so terminal output cannot corrupt the markdown fence.
   550	func sanitizeShellOutput(content string) string {
   551		content = strings.ReplaceAll(content, "\r\n", "\n")
   552		return strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
   553			if unicode.IsControl(r) && r != '\n' && r != '\t' {
   554				return -1
   555			}
   556			return r
   557		}, ansi.Strip(content))
   558	}
   559	
   560	// toolPathHints records the workspace paths a call touched, normalized
   561	// against the workspace root.
   562	func toolPathHints(name string, input map[string]any, workspaceRoot string) []string {
   563		var hints []string
   564		add := func(path string) {
   565			if path = strings.TrimSpace(path); path == "" {
   566				return
   567			}
   568			if normalized := spi.NormalizePath(path, workspaceRoot); normalized != "" {
   569				hints = append(hints, normalized)
   570			}
   571		}
   572	
   573		switch spi.NormalizeToolName(name) {
   574		case toolRead, toolWrite, toolEdit:
   575			add(spi.StringValue(input, "path"))
   576		case toolGlob, toolGrep:
   577			add(spi.StringValue(input, "path"))
   578		case toolShell:
   579			cwd := spi.StringValue(input, "workdir")
   580			if cwd == "" {
   581				cwd = workspaceRoot
   582			}
   583			hints = append(hints, spi.ExtractShellPathHints(spi.StringValue(input, "command"), cwd, workspaceRoot)...)
   584		}
   585	
   586		if len(hints) == 0 {
   587			return nil
   588		}
   589		slices.Sort(hints)
   590		return slices.Compact(hints)
   591	}

    20	// Watcher timing. Package variables so tests can shorten them.

    22		// debounceDelay collapses the burst of WAL writes one streamed update
    23		// produces into a single read, taken after the burst's last write.
    24		debounceDelay = 300 * time.Millisecond
    25	
    26		// maxBurstDelay bounds how long a continuous burst (a long streaming
    27		// response) can postpone a read, so the markdown keeps growing while the
    28		// agent is still writing.
    29		maxBurstDelay = 2 * time.Second

    31		// reconcileInterval is the periodic re-read that recovers from missed
    32		// filesystem events. One indexed query per interval.

    39	// sessionWatcher follows one project's sessions in OpenCode's database and
    40	// delivers each new or changed session, in order, on a single worker.
    41	//
    42	// OpenCode keeps every session in one SQLite database, so the watch is a fixed
    43	// set of one directory (the database's, or its nearest existing ancestor
    44	// until OpenCode creates it) no matter how many sessions accumulate.
    45	type sessionWatcher struct {
    46		projectPath string

    48		callback    func(*spi.AgentChatSession)
    49		dbPath      string
    50		dbDir       string

    56		// form the baseline; anything written at or after it is activity.
    57		startMillis int64
    58		// adoptExisting is set when the database did not exist at startup: every
    59		// session in a store that arrives later is new activity, even one whose
    60		// timestamps predate startup (a store copied or restored into place).
    61		adoptExisting bool
