    72	// startWatcher records the startup boundary, establishes the watch and starts
    73	// the worker. It returns an error only when no watch can be established at all.
    74	func startWatcher(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, callback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) (*sessionWatcher, error) {
    75		if callback == nil {
    76			return nil, errors.New("session callback must not be nil")
    77		}
    78		dbPath, err := getDatabasePath()
    79		if err != nil {
    80			return nil, err
    81		}
    82	
    83		fsWatcher, err := fsnotify.NewWatcher()
    84		if err != nil {
    85			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create file watcher: %w", err)
    86		}
    87	
    88		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
    89		w := &sessionWatcher{
    90			projectPath: projectPath,
    91			debugRaw:    debugRaw,
    92			callback:    callback,
    93			dbPath:      dbPath,
    94			dbDir:       filepath.Dir(dbPath),
    95			fsWatcher:   fsWatcher,
    96			known:       make(map[string]signature),
    97			ctx:         ctx,
    98			cancel:      cancel,
    99		}
   100	
   101		// Whether the store exists is decided before the boundary is taken: a
   102		// store that appears at any point after this check arrived after startup
   103		// and is adopted whole, even when its rows carry older timestamps.
   104		switch _, statErr := os.Stat(dbPath); {
   105		case errors.Is(statErr, os.ErrNotExist):
   106			w.adoptExisting = true
   107		case statErr != nil:
   108			// The store may well exist; adopting it would republish its history
   109			// once it becomes readable, so the startup boundary still applies.
   110			slog.Warn("WatchAgent: Cannot inspect OpenCode database", "path", dbPath, "error", statErr)
   111		}
   112	
   113		// The boundary is taken before the watch exists, so a write that lands
   114		// while the watch is being set up or before the first read is newer than
   115		// the boundary and is emitted rather than absorbed into the baseline.
   116		w.startMillis = time.Now().UnixMilli()
   117	
   118		if err := w.updateWatch(); err != nil {
   119			cancel()
   120			_ = fsWatcher.Close() // nothing was delivered; the watch error is what matters
   121			return nil, err
   122		}
   123	
   124		if beforeFirstCheck != nil {
   125			beforeFirstCheck()
   126		}
   127	
   128		if _, err := os.Stat(dbPath); err == nil {
   129			// OpenCode's database is normally in WAL mode already; this makes sure
   130			// every write reaches the -wal file the watch relies on.
   131			if err := spi.EnsureWALMode(dbPath); err != nil {
   132				slog.Warn("WatchAgent: Failed to ensure WAL mode on OpenCode database", "path", dbPath, "error", err)
   133			}
   134		}
   135	
   136		slog.Info("OpenCode watcher started",
   137			"projectPath", projectPath,
   138			"dbPath", dbPath,
   139			"watchedDir", w.watchedDir,
   140			"storeExists", !w.adoptExisting)
   141	
   142		w.wg.Go(w.run)
   143		return w, nil
   144	}
   145	
   146	// beforeFirstCheck, when set by a test, runs after the boundary and the watch
   147	// are established and before the first read, where real activity (a write, or
   148	// a store created or restored) can race the startup.
   149	var beforeFirstCheck func()
   150	
   151	// Stop ends the watch after delivering any change that has not been delivered
   152	// yet. Safe to call more than once.
   153	func (w *sessionWatcher) Stop() {
   154		w.stopOnce.Do(func() {
   155			slog.Info("Stopping OpenCode watcher")
   156			w.cancel()
   157			w.wg.Wait()
   158			if err := w.fsWatcher.Close(); err != nil {
   159				slog.Debug("Failed to close OpenCode file watcher", "error", err)
   160			}
   161			slog.Info("OpenCode watcher stopped")
   162		})
   163	}
   164	
   165	// run is the single worker: it owns the known map, the watch, and every
   166	// callback, so deliveries are ordered and shutdown has one thing to join.
   167	func (w *sessionWatcher) run() {
   168		reconcile := time.NewTicker(reconcileInterval)
   169		defer reconcile.Stop()
   170	
   171		debounce := time.NewTimer(debounceDelay)
   172		debounce.Stop()
   173		var debounceC <-chan time.Time
   174		var burstStart time.Time
   175	
   176		events := w.fsWatcher.Events
   177		watchErrors := w.fsWatcher.Errors
   178	
   179		// The first read records the baseline and delivers anything written
   180		// since the boundary.
   181		w.check("startup")
   182	
   183		for {
   184			select {
   185			case <-w.ctx.Done():
   186				debounce.Stop()
   187				w.check("shutdown")
   188				return
   189	
   190			case event, ok := <-events:
   191				if !ok {
   192					events = nil
   193					continue
   194				}
   195				if !w.handleEvent(event) {
   196					continue
   197				}
   198				now := time.Now()
   199				if debounceC == nil {
   200					burstStart = now
   201				}
   202				wait := min(debounceDelay, max(maxBurstDelay-now.Sub(burstStart), 0))
   203				debounce.Reset(wait)
   204				debounceC = debounce.C
   205	
   206			case <-debounceC:
   207				debounceC = nil
   208				w.check("file-change")
   209	
   210			case <-reconcile.C:
   211				if w.watchedDir != w.dbDir {
   212					// Recovers a missed directory-creation event.
   213					if err := w.updateWatch(); err != nil {
   214						slog.Debug("OpenCode watcher: Failed to update watch", "error", err)
   215					}
   216				}
   217				w.check("reconcile")
   218	
   219			case err, ok := <-watchErrors:
   220				if !ok {
   221					watchErrors = nil
   222					continue
   223				}
   224				slog.Warn("OpenCode watcher: File watch error", "error", err)
   225			}
   226		}
   227	}
   228	
   229	// handleEvent reacts to one filesystem event and reports whether the
   230	// database may have changed.
   231	func (w *sessionWatcher) handleEvent(event fsnotify.Event) bool {
   232		slog.Debug("OpenCode watcher: File event", "path", event.Name, "op", event.Op)
   233	
   234		if w.watchedDir != w.dbDir {
   235			// Waiting for OpenCode to create its data directory: follow each
   236			// directory it creates on the way down.
   237			if event.Has(fsnotify.Create) {
   238				if err := w.updateWatch(); err != nil {
   239					slog.Warn("OpenCode watcher: Failed to follow new directory", "path", event.Name, "error", err)
   240				}
   241			}
   242			return w.watchedDir == w.dbDir
   243		}
   244	
   245		if event.Name == w.dbDir && (event.Has(fsnotify.Remove) || event.Has(fsnotify.Rename)) {
   246			// The data directory went away; fall back to waiting for it.
   247			if err := w.updateWatch(); err != nil {
   248				slog.Warn("OpenCode watcher: Failed to re-establish watch", "error", err)
   249			}
   250			return false
   251		}
   252	
   253		isDatabaseFile := event.Name == w.dbPath || strings.HasPrefix(event.Name, w.dbPath+"-")
   254		return isDatabaseFile && (event.Has(fsnotify.Write) || event.Has(fsnotify.Create))
   255	}
   256	
   257	// updateWatch points the single directory watch at the database's directory,
   258	// or at its nearest existing ancestor until that directory exists, so the
   259	// watcher never disables itself because OpenCode has not run yet.
   260	func (w *sessionWatcher) updateWatch() error {
   261		target := nearestExistingDir(w.dbDir)
   262		if target == w.watchedDir {
   263			return nil
   264		}
   265		if err := w.fsWatcher.Add(target); err != nil {
   266			return fmt.Errorf("failed to watch %s: %w", target, err)
   267		}
   268		if w.watchedDir != "" {
   269			// The previous directory may already be gone; its watch is dead either way.
   270			_ = w.fsWatcher.Remove(w.watchedDir)
   271		}
   272		slog.Debug("OpenCode watcher: Watching directory", "dir", target, "waitingForStore", target != w.dbDir)
   273		w.watchedDir = target
   274		return nil
   275	}
   276	
   277	// predatesStart reports whether every write to the session happened before
   278	// the watcher started.
   279	func (w *sessionWatcher) predatesStart(summary sessionSummary) bool {
   280		return summary.TimeUpdated < w.startMillis && summary.LastMessageUpdate < w.startMillis
   281	}
   282	
   283	// nearestExistingDir returns path if it is an existing directory, otherwise
   284	// its closest existing ancestor.
   285	func nearestExistingDir(path string) string {
   286		for {
   287			if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
   288				return path
   289			}
   290			parent := filepath.Dir(path)
   291			if parent == path {
   292				return path
   293			}
   294			path = parent
   295		}
   296	}
   297	
   298	// check reads the project's sessions and delivers each one whose signature
   299	// changed since it was last delivered or baselined. A session seen for the
   300	// first time joins the baseline instead when its last write predates startup,
   301	// whichever check first reads it, so a failed or late first read cannot
   302	// republish history.
   303	//
   304	// Updates are collected first and delivered after the database is closed, so
   305	// a slow callback (a markdown write, a cloud sync) never holds the connection.
   306	func (w *sessionWatcher) check(trigger string) {
   307		var updates []*spi.AgentChatSession
   308		err := withDatabase(func(db *sql.DB) error {
   309			summaries, err := listSessionSummaries(db, w.projectPath)
   310			if err != nil {
   311				return err
   312			}
   313			for _, summary := range summaries {
   314				sig := summary.signature()
   315				known, seen := w.known[summary.ID]
   316				if seen && known == sig {
   317					continue
   318				}
   319				if !seen && !w.adoptExisting && w.predatesStart(summary) {
   320					w.known[summary.ID] = sig
   321					continue
   322				}
   323				snapshot, err := readSessionSnapshot(db, summary.ID)
   324				if err != nil {
   325					// Left unrecorded so the next check retries it.
   326					slog.Warn("OpenCode watcher: Failed to read session", "sessionId", summary.ID, "error", err)
   327					continue
   328				}
   329				session := convertSnapshot(snapshot, w.projectPath, w.debugRaw)
   330				if session == nil {
   331					// No prompt yet; retried once the first message lands.
   332					continue
   333				}
   334				w.known[summary.ID] = sig
   335				updates = append(updates, session)
   336			}
   337			return nil
   338		})
   339		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errNoDatabase) {
   340			slog.Warn("OpenCode watcher: Check failed", "trigger", trigger, "error", err)
   341		}
   342		for _, session := range updates {
   343			slog.Info("OpenCode watcher: Delivering session update",
   344				"sessionId", session.SessionID, "trigger", trigger)
   345			spi.DeliverSession(watcherLabel, w.callback, session)
   346		}
   347		slog.Debug("OpenCode watcher: Check complete", "trigger", trigger, "delivered", len(updates))
   348	}
     1	package opencode
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"bytes"
     5		"errors"
     6		"fmt"
     7		"log/slog"
     8		"os"
     9		"os/exec"
    10		"path/filepath"
    11		"strings"
    12	
    13		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
    14	)
    15	
    16	// defaultOpenCodeCommand is used when no custom command is configured.
    17	const defaultOpenCodeCommand = "opencode"
    18	
    19	// sessionFlag and sessionFlagShort are OpenCode's flags for continuing a
    20	// session by id (`opencode --session <id>`, `opencode -s <id>`).
    21	const (
    22		sessionFlag      = "--session"
    23		sessionFlagShort = "-s"
    24	)
    25	
    26	// importStagingDir is where a reconstructed session waits to be imported,
    27	// under the user's cache directory. OpenCode reads sessions only from its
    28	// database, through its own service, so a reconstructed session is handed over
    29	// as an export file and loaded with `opencode session import`.
    30	var importStagingDir = []string{"specstory", "opencode-import"}
    31	
    32	// parseOpenCodeCommand splits a custom command into executable and arguments.
    33	func parseOpenCodeCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
    34		if customCommand != "" {
    35			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
    36			if len(parts) > 0 {
    37				return parts[0], parts[1:]
    38			}
    39		}
    40		return defaultOpenCodeCommand, nil
    41	}
    42	
    43	// stagedImportDirPath returns the staging directory without creating it.
    44	func stagedImportDirPath() (string, error) {
    45		cacheDir, err := os.UserCacheDir()
    46		if err != nil {
    47			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve the user cache directory: %w", err)
    48		}
    49		return filepath.Join(append([]string{cacheDir}, importStagingDir...)...), nil
    50	}
    51	
    52	// stagedImportDir returns the staging directory, creating it private to the
    53	// user. The staged file holds a whole conversation, and a fixed name in a
    54	// shared temp directory could be read, or pre-created, by another local user.
    55	func stagedImportDir() (string, error) {
    56		dir, err := stagedImportDirPath()
    57		if err != nil {
    58			return "", err
    59		}
    60		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
    61			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create %s: %w", dir, err)
    62		}
    63		// MkdirAll leaves an existing directory's mode alone.
    64		if err := os.Chmod(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
    65			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to restrict %s: %w", dir, err)
    66		}
    67		return dir, nil
    68	}
    69	
    70	// stagedImportPath returns where a reconstructed session named filename is
    71	// staged for import.
    72	func stagedImportPath(filename string) (string, error) {
    73		dir, err := stagedImportDir()
    74		if err != nil {
    75			return "", err
    76		}
    77		return filepath.Join(dir, filename), nil
    78	}
    79	
    80	// stagedImportFilename is the staging filename for a reconstructed session.
    81	func stagedImportFilename(sessionID string) string {
    82		return sessionID + ".json"
    83	}
    84	
    85	// importStagedSession loads a reconstructed session into OpenCode when one is
    86	// staged for sessionID, then removes the staged file. Sessions that were not
    87	// reconstructed have nothing staged and are left alone.
    88	//
    89	// Only the executable of a custom command is used: its arguments configure an
    90	// interactive launch and do not apply to the import subcommand.
    91	func importStagedSession(customCommand, projectPath, sessionID string) error {
    92		// Only a plain id can name a staged file; anything with a path element in
    93		// it was not minted by ReconstructSession.
    94		if sessionID == "" || sessionID != filepath.Base(sessionID) || strings.ContainsAny(sessionID, `/\`) {
    95			return nil
    96		}
    97		// Looking for a staged file must not create the staging directory as a
    98		// side effect of every resume.
    99		dir, err := stagedImportDirPath()
   100		if err != nil {
   101			return err
   102		}
   103		stagedPath := filepath.Join(dir, stagedImportFilename(sessionID))
   104		if _, err := os.Stat(stagedPath); err != nil {
   105			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
   106				return nil
   107			}
   108			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read staged OpenCode session %s: %w", stagedPath, err)
   109		}
   110	
   111		command, _ := parseOpenCodeCommand(customCommand)
   112		args := []string{"session", "import", "--directory", projectPath, stagedPath}
   113		slog.Info("importStagedSession: Importing reconstructed session into OpenCode",
   114			"command", command, "args", args, "sessionId", sessionID)
   115	
   116		cmd := exec.Command(command, args...)
   117		var output bytes.Buffer
   118		cmd.Stdout = &output
   119		cmd.Stderr = &output
   120		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
   121			slog.Error("importStagedSession: OpenCode import failed",
   122				"sessionId", sessionID, "error", err, "output", strings.TrimSpace(output.String()))
   123			return fmt.Errorf("failed to import the reconstructed session into OpenCode (%s %s): %w\n%s",
   124				command, strings.Join(args, " "), err, strings.TrimSpace(output.String()))
   125		}
   126		slog.Info("importStagedSession: Imported reconstructed session", "sessionId", sessionID,
   127			"output", strings.TrimSpace(output.String()))
   128	
   129		if err := os.Remove(stagedPath); err != nil {
   130			// The import succeeded. A leftover file is harmless: importing an id
   131			// that already exists is a no-op ("Session already exists", exit 0,
   132			// observed with 2.0.14).
   133			slog.Warn("importStagedSession: Failed to remove staged session", "path", stagedPath, "error", err)
   134		}
   135		return nil
   136	}
   137	
   138	// executeOpenCode runs OpenCode attached to the terminal, continuing
   139	// resumeSessionID when one is given, and returns its exit status as an
   140	// spi.AgentExitError so the caller can finish saving before exiting.
   141	func executeOpenCode(customCommand, projectPath, resumeSessionID string) error {
   142		command, args := parseOpenCodeCommand(customCommand)
   143		// A requested session wins over one pinned in the configured command.
   144		args = spi.EnsureResumeFlagArgs(args, resumeSessionID, sessionFlag, sessionFlagShort)
   145	
   146		cmd := exec.Command(command, args...)
   147		// OpenCode records the directory it runs in as the session's project;
   148		// running it in the project keeps a --project-path run's sessions where
   149		// the watcher looks for them.
   150		cmd.Dir = projectPath
   151		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
   152		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
   153		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
   154	
   155		slog.Info("executeOpenCode: Starting OpenCode process",
   156			"command", command, "args", args, "projectPath", projectPath)
   157		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
   158			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start opencode: %w", err)
   159		}
   160	
   161		slog.Info("executeOpenCode: Waiting for OpenCode to exit")
   162		if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
   163			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
   164			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
   165				exitCode := exitErr.ExitCode()
   166				slog.Info("executeOpenCode: OpenCode exited", "exitCode", exitCode)
   167				return &spi.AgentExitError{Agent: providerName, Code: exitCode}
   168			}
   169			return fmt.Errorf("opencode execution failed: %w", err)
   170		}
   171	
   172		slog.Info("executeOpenCode: OpenCode exited normally", "exitCode", 0)
   173		return nil
   174	}
     1	package opencode
     2	
     3	import (
     4		"crypto/rand"
     5		"encoding/json"
     6		"errors"
     7		"fmt"
     8		"math/big"
     9		"sync"
    10		"time"
    11	
    12		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
    13		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
    14	)
    15	
    16	// Id prefixes OpenCode uses for sessions and messages.
    17	const (
    18		sessionIDPrefix = "ses_"
    19		messageIDPrefix = "msg_"
    20	)
    21	
    22	// idRandomLength and idAlphabet describe the random tail of an OpenCode id:
    23	// 14 base62 characters, as observed in ids written by 2.0.14.
    24	const (
    25		idRandomLength = 14
    26		idAlphabet     = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    27	)
    28	
    29	// exportInfo is the session header of OpenCode's export format, the input to
    30	// `opencode session import`.
    31	type exportInfo struct {
    32		ID string `json:"id"`
    33		// ProjectID is required by the import schema but replaced by the project
    34		// OpenCode resolves for --directory, so it is left empty.
    35		ProjectID string         `json:"projectID"`
    36		Title     string         `json:"title"`
    37		Cost      float64        `json:"cost"`
    38		Tokens    tokenUsage     `json:"tokens"`
    39		Time      exportTime     `json:"time"`
    40		Location  exportLocation `json:"location"`
    41		Metadata  map[string]any `json:"metadata"`
    42	}
    43	
    44	type exportTime struct {
    45		Created int64 `json:"created"`
    46		Updated int64 `json:"updated"`
    47	}
    48	
    49	type exportLocation struct {
    50		Directory string `json:"directory"`
    51	}
    52	
    53	// exportMessage is one record of the export format. User records carry Text;
    54	// assistant records carry Agent, Model, Content and Finish.
    55	type exportMessage struct {
    56		ID      string           `json:"id"`
    57		Type    string           `json:"type"`
    58		Time    recordTime       `json:"time"`
    59		Text    string           `json:"text,omitempty"`
    60		Agent   *string          `json:"agent,omitempty"`
    61		Model   *modelRef        `json:"model,omitempty"`
    62		Content []exportTextPart `json:"content,omitempty"`
    63		Finish  string           `json:"finish,omitempty"`
    64	}
    65	
    66	type exportTextPart struct {
    67		Type string `json:"type"`
    68		Text string `json:"text"`
    69	}
    70	
    71	type exportDocument struct {
    72		Info     exportInfo      `json:"info"`
    73		Messages []exportMessage `json:"messages"`
    74	}
    75	
    76	// ReconstructSession rebuilds a session as an OpenCode export document from
    77	// the neutral SessionData. It does not touch OpenCode's database: the resume
    78	// flow writes the document to NativeSessionPath, and ExecAgentAndWatch loads
    79	// it with `opencode session import` before launching `opencode -s <id>`.
    80	func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
    81		turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
    82		if err != nil {
    83			return nil, err
    84		}
    85		workspaceRoot := spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts, data)
    86		if workspaceRoot == "" {
    87			return nil, errors.New("cannot reconstruct an OpenCode session without a workspace root")
    88		}
    89	
    90		now := time.Now()
    91		sessionID := newOpenCodeID(sessionIDPrefix, now, true)
    92		// One millisecond apart, ending now, so records keep their order without
    93		// dating any of them in the future.
    94		firstMillis := now.UnixMilli() - int64(len(turns))
    95	
    96		// Imported turns name no agent or model: they were not produced by an
    97		// OpenCode agent. OpenCode accepts empty values and uses the project's
    98		// configured agent and model for the next prompt.
    99		emptyAgent := ""
   100		messages := make([]exportMessage, 0, len(turns))
   101		for i, turn := range turns {
   102			created := firstMillis + int64(i)
   103			message := exportMessage{
   104				ID:   newOpenCodeID(messageIDPrefix, time.UnixMilli(created), false),
   105				Time: recordTime{Created: created},
   106			}
   107			if turn.Role == schema.RoleUser {
   108				message.Type = recordUser
   109				message.Text = turn.Text
   110			} else {
   111				message.Type = recordAssistant
   112				message.Time.Completed = created
   113				message.Agent = &emptyAgent
   114				message.Model = &modelRef{}
   115				message.Content = []exportTextPart{{Type: partText, Text: turn.Text}}
   116				message.Finish = "stop"
   117			}
   118			messages = append(messages, message)
   119		}
   120	
   121		document := exportDocument{
   122			Info: exportInfo{
   123				ID:    sessionID,
   124				Title: spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data.Slug),
   125				Time:  exportTime{Created: firstMillis, Updated: now.UnixMilli()},
   126				Location: exportLocation{
   127					Directory: workspaceRoot,
   128				},
   129				Metadata: map[string]any{"specstorySourceSessionId": data.SessionID},
   130			},
   131			Messages: messages,
   132		}
   133	
   134		content, err := json.MarshalIndent(document, "", "  ")
   135		if err != nil {
   136			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode OpenCode export document: %w", err)
   137		}
   138		return &spi.ReconstructedSession{
   139			SessionID: sessionID,
   140			Filename:  stagedImportFilename(sessionID),
   141			Content:   content,
   142		}, nil
   143	}
   144	
   145	// NativeSessionPath returns where the export document is staged. OpenCode has
   146	// no per-session files; ExecAgentAndWatch imports the staged document into
   147	// OpenCode's database before launching the resumed session. The staging
   148	// directory is created here, private to the user, because the caller would
   149	// otherwise create it world-readable.
   150	func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(_ string, filename string) (string, error) {
   151		return stagedImportPath(filename)
   152	}
   153	
   154	// SupportsReconstruction reports true: ReconstructSession produces a session
   155	// OpenCode can import and continue.
   156	func (p *Provider) SupportsReconstruction() bool {
   157		return true
   158	}
   159	
   160	// idMutex guards idLastMillis and idLastCounter, which disambiguate ids minted
   161	// within the same millisecond the way OpenCode's own generator does.
   162	var (
   163		idMutex       sync.Mutex
   164		idLastMillis  int64
   165		idLastCounter int64
   166	)
   167	
   168	// newOpenCodeID mints an id in OpenCode's layout: prefix, 12 hex digits of
   169	// (unix-ms << 12 | counter), then 14 random base62 characters. Session ids
   170	// invert the hex (descending) so newer sessions sort first, as OpenCode's do.
   171	func newOpenCodeID(prefix string, at time.Time, descending bool) string {
   172		idMutex.Lock()
   173		millis := at.UnixMilli()
   174		if millis == idLastMillis {
   175			idLastCounter++
   176		} else {
   177			idLastMillis = millis
   178			idLastCounter = 0
   179		}
   180		value := (millis << 12) | (idLastCounter & 0xfff)
   181		idMutex.Unlock()
   182	
   183		const mask = (int64(1) << 48) - 1
   184		if descending {
   185			value = ^value
   186		}
   187		return fmt.Sprintf("%s%012x%s", prefix, value&mask, randomBase62(idRandomLength))
   188	}
   189	
   190	func randomBase62(length int) string {
   191		alphabetSize := big.NewInt(int64(len(idAlphabet)))
   192		result := make([]byte, length)
   193		for i := range result {
   194			n, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, alphabetSize)
   195			if err != nil {
   196				// crypto/rand does not fail on supported platforms; fall back to
   197				// the first letter rather than aborting a resume over it.
   198				result[i] = idAlphabet[0]
   199				continue
   200			}
   201			result[i] = idAlphabet[n.Int64()]
   202		}
   203		return string(result)
   204	}

=== FORMAT ===
# OpenCode Session Format

OpenCode (`opencode`, the open source terminal coding agent) keeps every session in one SQLite database owned by a background service. Everything below was verified empirically against OpenCode 2.0.14 on macOS by driving the binary (TUI, `opencode run`, `opencode session import`) and reading what it wrote.

Baseline version, exactly as `opencode --version` prints it:

```text
opencode v2.0.14
```

## Store layout

```text
$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/            (default ~/.local/share/opencode on every OS)
├── opencode.db                     # all projects, sessions and messages
├── opencode.db-wal                 # write-ahead log; nearly every write lands here first
├── opencode.db-shm
├── log/opencode.log
├── shell/<project-id>/             # spill files for user shell commands
└── snapshot/, repos/, tool-output/ # file snapshots and caches, not transcripts
```

- The data directory is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode`, falling back to `~/.local/share/opencode`. OpenCode computes it the same way on macOS, Linux and Windows (`os.homedir()` joined with `.local/share`); there is no `%APPDATA%` branch. `opencode debug paths` prints it.
- The database file name is `$OPENCODE_DB` when set (resolved relative to the data directory; `:memory:` keeps no file), otherwise `opencode.db` for the `latest`, `dev`, `beta`, `next` and `prod` release channels, or when `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CHANNEL_DB` is `1`/`true`. Other channels use `opencode-<channel>.db`. Released builds report `channel=latest` in their log.
- The database is in WAL mode already. `opencode serve --service` (started automatically by the TUI and every CLI subcommand) is the only writer; the TUI and `opencode run` talk to it over HTTP.
- `account`, `control_account` and `credential` hold OAuth tokens and API keys. They are never read.

## Tables that matter

| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| `session_v2` | One row per session. `directory` is the working directory the session was started in (the project association and reindex's origin). `parent_id` is set for subagent sessions. `title` is OpenCode's own generated title (empty until the title model answers). `slug` is a random two-word label (`cosmic-wolf`), not derived from content. `version` is the OpenCode version that created the session. `time_created` / `time_updated` are Unix milliseconds. |
| `session_message` | One row per conversation record: `id`, `session_id`, `type`, `seq`, `time_created`, `time_updated`, and `data` (JSON text). Ordered by `seq` within a session. `seq` values are sparse (they share a counter with other session events), so gaps are normal. |
| `project` | `id`, `worktree`. The id is the repository's root commit hash for a git worktree, otherwise an opaque generated id (and `global` for some directories). Not used for matching: `session_v2.directory` is authoritative. |
| `event_sequence` | The next sequence number per session aggregate. Maintained by OpenCode; never written by this provider. |
| everything else | Permissions, instructions, workspaces, worktrees, inbox/pending queues, key-value settings. Not transcripts. |

## Message records

`session_message.type` selects the shape of `data`. The complete set in 2.0.14's OpenAPI schema (`Session.Message.Info`) is below; every kind marked "observed" was produced and inspected in a real session.

| type | Observed | Content | Rendered as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | yes | `text`, `files[]` (attachments: `mime`, `name`, `source`, `data`), `agents[]` (`@agent` mentions), `skills[]` | A user message. Slash commands are expanded before storage: `/review` is stored as a `user` record whose `text` is the whole command template, with no marker naming the command. |
| `assistant` | yes | One model step: `agent`, `model` (`{id, providerID, variant}`), `content[]` parts, `finish`, `error`, `tokens`, `cost`, `time.{created,streamed,completed}` | Agent messages, one per content part, in part order. |
| `shell` | yes | A user `!command`: `shellID`, `command`, `status` (`running`, `exited`, `timeout`, `killed`), `exit`, `output.{output,truncated}` | A user message labeled "User ran a shell command" with the command, output and exit status. |
| `synthetic` | yes | Text OpenCode injects for the model: the output echo of a user shell command (`metadata.source == "shell"`) and Plan-mode `<system-reminder>` blocks | Not rendered: scaffolding. The shell echo duplicates the `shell` record. |
| `compaction` | yes | `status` (`running`, `completed`, `failed`), `reason` (`auto`, `manual`), `summary`, `recent`, `error` | A completed compaction renders its summary as an agent message; a failed one renders its error. A running one is not rendered until it completes. |
| `idle` | yes | `outcome` (`succeeded`, `failed`, `interrupted`): the end of a turn | Not rendered: lifecycle marker. |
| `agent-switched` | yes | `agent`, `previous` (for example `build` → `plan`) | Not rendered: the agent is recorded on each assistant step. |
| `model-switched` | yes | `model`, `previous` | Not rendered: the model is recorded on each assistant step. |
| `system` | no | `text`, `description` | Not rendered: scaffolding. |
| `skill` | no | `skill`, `name`, `text` (an injected skill body) | Not rendered: scaffolding (the skill body is instructions, not conversation). |
| `location-switched` | no | `location.directory`, `projectID`, `subpath` | Not rendered: metadata. |

An unfamiliar `type` is logged at Debug and skipped; its row is still preserved in `RawData` and the debug export.

### Assistant content parts

| part `type` | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `text`, `state.itemId` | Whitespace-only text parts occur between tool calls and are skipped. |
| `reasoning` | `text`, `state`, `time` | Thinking. Some providers return only encrypted reasoning (`state.reasoningEncryptedContent`) with an empty `text`; only non-empty `text` is rendered. |
| `tool` | `id` (the call id), `name`, `executed`, `state`, `time.{created,ran,completed}` | The call and its result live in the same part, so no pairing is needed. One assistant step can hold several tool parts (parallel calls). |

Tool `state` by `status`:

| status | Fields |
|---|---|
| `streaming` | `input` is the partial argument string |
| `running` | `input` object, `metadata` |
| `completed` | `input` object, `content[]`, `metadata` |
| `error` | `input` object, `error.{type,message}`, optional `content[]` |

`content[]` items are `{type: "text", text}` or `{type: "file", uri, mime, name}`. A completed call can still report failure inside its text: `execute` returns the thrown error as its result with status `completed`.

An assistant step that fails before producing content has `finish: "error"`, an empty `content`, and `error.message` (for example an invalid model id); it renders as an agent error message.

## Tool shapes observed

Tool names are stored bare (`read`, not `functions.read`). The inventory and the calls below come from 2.0.14 with the `build` agent and the default configuration.

| Tool | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | `path` (relative or absolute, file or directory), optional `offset`, `limit` | Text: `Read file <path>, lines a-b` then `N: <line>` rows, or `Read directory <path>, entries a-b` then one entry per line. Missing file: status `error`, `File not found: <path>`. |
| `write` | `path`, `content` | Text acknowledgement (`Created file successfully: <path>`). |
| `edit` | `path`, `oldString`, `newString` | Text acknowledgement; `metadata.files[]` carries a unified diff per file (`patch`, `additions`, `deletions`). |
| `glob` | `pattern`, optional `path` | Newline-separated absolute paths; `metadata.count`. |
| `grep` | `pattern`, optional `path`, `include` | `Found N matches` then per-file `Line N:` rows; `metadata.matches`. |
| `shell` | `command`, optional `workdir`, `timeout` (milliseconds) | Output text, then a separate `Command exited with code N.` text item for the model; `metadata.exit`. |
| `webfetch` | `url`, optional `format` (`html` observed) | The page converted to markdown, or raw HTML with `format: "html"`. |
| `websearch` | `query` | Only failures were observed (`Web search cancelled`, status `error`). |
| `skill` | `id` | `<skill_content name="...">` wrapping the skill document; `metadata.name`, `metadata.directory`. |
| `subagent` | `agent`, `description`, `prompt` | `<subagent sessionID="..." state="completed">` wrapping the subagent's final answer; `metadata.sessionID`. The subagent's own conversation is a child session (`parent_id` set). |
| `question` | `questions[]`: `{question, header, options[]: {label, description}}` | Text restating the answers for the model; `metadata.answers` holds the chosen labels per question. Only asked in the interactive TUI, which shows a form. |
| `execute` | `code` (JavaScript run in OpenCode's "Code Mode" sandbox, calling `search()` and `tools.<path>(...)`) | The returned value as text, or the thrown error as text; `metadata.toolCalls[]` lists each inner call's `tool`, `status` and `input`. |

## Write lifecycle

- The `user` row is inserted when the prompt is submitted.
- Each model step inserts an `assistant` row as soon as it starts and rewrites that same row in place while parts stream in; `time_updated` advances on every rewrite. A new step (after tool calls) inserts a new `assistant` row.
- An `idle` row closes the turn.
- The title is generated asynchronously and written to `session_v2.title`, which also advances `session_v2.time_updated` without touching any message row.
- A session therefore changes when its `session_v2.time_updated`, its message count, or its newest message `time_updated` changes. All three are read in one query.
- Every write goes through SQLite's WAL, so `opencode.db-wal` is created or written on each change. SQLite may delete and recreate the WAL at checkpoints, so the data directory is watched rather than the file.
- Nothing is transient: there are no scratch files for in-flight messages. A partially streamed assistant step is visible in its row until it completes.

## Project association

`session_v2.directory` is the realpath of the directory OpenCode was started in (on macOS `/tmp/x` is recorded as `/private/tmp/x`). A session belongs to a project when that directory equals the project's canonical path. Subagent sessions (`parent_id` set) are part of their parent's conversation and are not listed on their own, matching `opencode session list`, which shows only top-level sessions.

## Version

`session_v2.version` records the OpenCode version that created the session. There is no per-message version.

## Resume

- Native resume is `opencode -s <session-id>` (TUI) or `opencode run -s <session-id> <message>` (headless). New records append to the same session.
- OpenCode reads a session only from the database, through its service. There is no per-session file to write.
- `opencode session import --directory <dir> <file.json>` loads a session in OpenCode's export format (`opencode session export <id>` produces it) through the service, which assigns the project for `<dir>` (creating it if the directory is new), numbers `seq` from 1 in array order, and initializes `event_sequence`. The session id in the file is preserved.
- The import schema requires `info.id`, `info.projectID` (any string: it is replaced by the project resolved from `--directory`), `info.cost`, `info.tokens`, `info.time.created`, `info.time.updated`, `info.location.directory`, and each message's `id`, `type`, `time.created`. A user message needs `text`; an assistant message needs `agent`, `model` and `content`.

### Reconstructed sessions

A reconstructed session is an export document with the flattened turns: user turns become `user` records, agent turns become `assistant` records with one `text` part and `finish: "stop"`. Verified with a minimal document containing a passphrase: `opencode -s <id>` opened it with both turns visible, answered "What is the magic passphrase?" from the imported context, and appended `agent-switched`, `model-switched`, `user`, `assistant` and `idle` records to the same session.

- Assistant records require `agent` and `model`; reconstructed records write `""` and `{"id": "", "providerID": ""}` because imported turns were not produced by an OpenCode agent or model. OpenCode accepts both, labels the imported turns with an empty agent and model, and uses the project's configured agent and model for the next prompt.
- `info.projectID` is required but replaced on import, so it is written empty.
- `info.cost` and `info.tokens` are required and written as zero: the flattened transcript carries no usage.
- `info.metadata.specstorySourceSessionId` carries the source session id.
- Ids use OpenCode's layout: a `ses_` or `msg_` prefix, 12 hex digits of `(unix-ms << 12 | counter)` (bit-inverted for session ids so newer sessions sort first), and 14 random base62 characters.
- OpenCode's free "Zen" models refuse to continue any conversation whose assistant turns were not produced through Zen (`OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`, HTTP 403). This applies to every imported history, not to the reconstruction format: the same session continues normally with any other configured provider.
- `opencode run -s <id>` stalls on the first prompt sent to a freshly imported session and succeeds on the next attempt; the TUI (`opencode -s <id>`, which `specstory resume` launches) is not affected.

## What is not preserved

- `user.files[].data` (base64 attachment bodies) is not rendered; attachments render by name and MIME type.
- Encrypted reasoning, provider state, snapshots, costs and the `recent` field of compactions are not rendered. They remain in `RawData` and the debug export.
- The command name of an expanded slash command is not recorded by OpenCode, so the template text renders as the user's prompt and cannot be filtered from resumed transcripts.

   258		for _, field := range []string{`"providerState"`, `"reasoningEncryptedContent"`, `"idle_outcome"`} {
   259			if !strings.Contains(session.RawData, field) {
   260				t.Errorf("RawData dropped %s", field)

   308	// then fails: the error must not be stamped earlier than the part before it.
   309	func TestConvertStepErrorFollowsItsParts(t *testing.T) {

   311		project := newProjectDir(t, "project")
   312		insertSession(t, db, "ses_fail", project, 1000, 9000)

   314		insertMessage(t, db, "ses_fail", "msg_2", recordAssistant, 2, 2000,
   315			`{"time":{"created":2000},"agent":"build","model":{"id":"m","providerID":"p"},
   316			  "content":[{"type":"reasoning","text":"thinking first","time":{"created":5000}}],
   317			  "finish":"error","error":{"type":"provider.overloaded","message":"Overloaded"}}`)
   318	
   319		session, err := NewProvider().GetAgentChatSession(project, "ses_fail", false)
   320		if err != nil || session == nil {
   321			t.Fatalf("GetAgentChatSession() = %v, %v", session, err)
   322		}
   323		messages := allMessages(session.SessionData)
   324		last := messages[len(messages)-1]
   325		if messageText(last) != "[error] Overloaded" {
   326			t.Fatalf("last message = %q, want the step error", messageText(last))
   327		}
   328		if last.Timestamp < messages[len(messages)-2].Timestamp {
   329			t.Errorf("error at %s precedes the part before it at %s", last.Timestamp, messages[len(messages)-2].Timestamp)
   330		}
   331	}

    37	// useFixtureStore points OpenCode's data directory at a fresh temp directory
    38	// and returns the database path the provider will read.
    39	func useFixtureStore(t *testing.T) string {
    40		t.Helper()
    41		dataHome := t.TempDir()
    42		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", dataHome)
    43		t.Setenv(dbEnvVar, "")
    44		return filepath.Join(dataHome, dataDirName, defaultDBName)
    45	}
    46	
    47	// createFixtureDB creates dbPath with OpenCode 2.0.14's session tables (DDL
    48	// captured from a real database) and returns a read-write handle for tests
    49	// that write further records.
    50	func createFixtureDB(t *testing.T, dbPath string) *sql.DB {
    51		t.Helper()
    52		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dbPath), 0o755); err != nil {
    53			t.Fatal(err)
    54		}
    55		schema, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("testdata", "schema.sql"))
    56		if err != nil {
    57			t.Fatal(err)
    58		}
    59		// A running watcher may read the database while a test writes to it; the
    60		// busy timeout makes the writer wait for that reader instead of failing,
    61		// which Windows' mandatory file locking otherwise does immediately.
    62		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?"+spi.BusyTimeoutPragma)
    63		if err != nil {
    64			t.Fatal(err)
    65		}
    66		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
    67		t.Cleanup(func() { _ = db.Close() })
    68		if _, err := db.Exec(string(schema)); err != nil {
    69			t.Fatalf("create schema: %v", err)
    70		}
    71		return db
    72	}
    73	
    74	// readFixture loads captured records, rewriting each session's recorded
    75	// directory through dirs (fixture directory -> test directory).
    76	func readFixture(t *testing.T, name string, dirs map[string]string) []rawRecord {
    77		t.Helper()
    78		data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("testdata", name))
    79		if err != nil {
    80			t.Fatal(err)
    81		}
    82		var records []rawRecord
    83		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(bytes.NewReader(data))
    84		scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 1<<20), 16<<20)
    85		for scanner.Scan() {
    86			if len(bytes.TrimSpace(scanner.Bytes())) == 0 {
    87				continue
    88			}
    89			decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(scanner.Bytes()))
    90			decoder.UseNumber()
    91			var record rawRecord
    92			if err := decoder.Decode(&record); err != nil {
    93				t.Fatalf("decode %s: %v", name, err)
    94			}
    95			if record.Table == sessionTable {
    96				if dir, ok := record.Row["directory"].(string); ok {
    97					if mapped, ok := dirs[dir]; ok {
    98						record.Row["directory"] = mapped
    99					}
   100				}
   101			}
   102			records = append(records, record)
   103		}
   104		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
   105			t.Fatal(err)
   106		}
   107		return records
   108	}
   109	
   110	// insertRecords writes captured rows into the fixture database, column for
   111	// column, with message payloads stored as JSON text the way OpenCode stores
   112	// them.
   113	func insertRecords(t *testing.T, db *sql.DB, records []rawRecord) {
   114		t.Helper()
   115		for _, record := range records {
   116			columns := make([]string, 0, len(record.Row))
   117			for column := range record.Row {
   118				columns = append(columns, column)
   119			}
   120			slices.Sort(columns)
   121			values := make([]any, len(columns))
   122			for i, column := range columns {
   123				values[i] = sqlValue(t, column, record.Row[column])
   124			}
   125			query := fmt.Sprintf("INSERT INTO %s (%s) VALUES (%s)", record.Table,
   126				strings.Join(columns, ", "), strings.TrimSuffix(strings.Repeat("?, ", len(columns)), ", "))
   127			if _, err := db.Exec(query, values...); err != nil {
   128				t.Fatalf("insert into %s: %v", record.Table, err)
   129			}
   130		}
   131	}
   132	
   133	func sqlValue(t *testing.T, column string, value any) any {
   134		t.Helper()
   135		switch v := value.(type) {
   136		case json.Number:
   137			if i, err := v.Int64(); err == nil {
   138				return i
   139			}
   140			f, _ := v.Float64()
   141			return f
   142		case map[string]any, []any:
   143			// Only session_message.data holds a JSON document.
   144			encoded, err := json.Marshal(v)
   145			if err != nil {
   146				t.Fatalf("encode %s: %v", column, err)
   147			}
   148			return string(encoded)
   149		default:
   150			return v
   151		}
   152	}
   153	
   154	// loadFixtures creates the store and loads the named fixtures into it.
   155	func loadFixtures(t *testing.T, dirs map[string]string, names ...string) *sql.DB {
   156		t.Helper()
   157		db := createFixtureDB(t, useFixtureStore(t))
   158		for _, name := range names {
   159			insertRecords(t, db, readFixture(t, name, dirs))
   160		}
   161		return db
   162	}

    13	// renderedTool is one tool call as the provider renders it.
    14	type renderedTool struct {

    19	}
    20	
    21	// renderedTools converts a captured session through the real conversion path
    22	// and collects every rendered tool call.
    23	func renderedTools(t *testing.T, fixture, sessionID string) []renderedTool {
    24		t.Helper()
    25		session, _ := loadSession(t, sessionID, fixture)
    26		var tools []renderedTool
    27		for _, message := range allMessages(session.SessionData) {
    28			if message.Tool == nil {
    29				continue
    30			}
    31			tool := renderedTool{name: message.Tool.Name, input: message.Tool.Input}
    32			if message.Tool.Summary != nil {
    33				tool.summary = *message.Tool.Summary
    34			}
    35			if message.Tool.FormattedMarkdown != nil {
    36				tool.markdown = *message.Tool.FormattedMarkdown
    37			}
    38			tools = append(tools, tool)
    39		}
    40		return tools
    41	}

    43	// findTool returns the first rendered call to name whose input satisfies match.
    44	func findTool(t *testing.T, tools []renderedTool, name string, match func(map[string]any) bool) renderedTool {
    45		t.Helper()
    46		for _, tool := range tools {
    47			if tool.name == name && (match == nil || match(tool.input)) {
    48				return tool
    49			}
    50		}
    51		t.Fatalf("no rendered %s call matched", name)
    52		return renderedTool{}

   235	// TestToolInventorySweep checks every tool OpenCode 2.0.14 declares (see
   236	// testdata/tools.txt) has a deliberate classification, so a tool dropped from
   237	// the switch surfaces as a failure rather than as "unknown".
   238	func TestToolInventorySweep(t *testing.T) {
   239		want := map[string]string{
   240			"edit":      schema.ToolTypeWrite,
   241			"execute":   schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
   242			"question":  schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
   243			"glob":      schema.ToolTypeSearch,
   244			"grep":      schema.ToolTypeSearch,
   245			"read":      schema.ToolTypeRead,
   246			"shell":     schema.ToolTypeShell,
   247			"skill":     schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
   248			"subagent":  schema.ToolTypeGeneric,
   249			"webfetch":  schema.ToolTypeRead,
   250			"websearch": schema.ToolTypeSearch,
   251			"write":     schema.ToolTypeWrite,
   252		}
   253	
   254		file, err := os.Open(filepath.Join("testdata", "tools.txt"))
   255		if err != nil {
   256			t.Fatal(err)
   257		}
   258		defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()
   259	
   260		// tools.txt lists direct tools one per line until a blank line; the Code
   261		// Mode catalog after it is only reachable through execute.
   262		var declared []string
   263		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(file)
   264		for scanner.Scan() {
   265			line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
   266			if line == "" {
   267				break
   268			}
   269			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   270				continue
   271			}
   272			declared = append(declared, line)
   273		}
   274		if len(declared) != len(want) {
   275			t.Errorf("tools.txt declares %d direct tools %v, test expects %d", len(declared), declared, len(want))
   276		}
   277		for _, name := range declared {
   278			expected, ok := want[name]
   279			if !ok {
   280				t.Errorf("tools.txt tool %q has no expected type", name)
   281				continue
   282			}
   283			if got := toolType(name); got != expected {
   284				t.Errorf("toolType(%q) = %q, want %q", name, got, expected)
   285			}
   286		}
   287		if got := toolType("todowrite"); got != schema.ToolTypeUnknown {
   288			t.Errorf("an undeclared tool must stay unknown, got %q", got)
   289		}
   290	}

    72	func sessionIDs(sessions []spi.AgentChatSession) []string {

    74		for _, session := range sessions {

   141	func TestProjectReachedThroughOtherSpellings(t *testing.T) {

   158		if info, err := os.Stat(upper); err == nil && info.IsDir() {

   164		for name, spelling := range spellings {

   177	func TestCheck(t *testing.T) {
   178		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
   179			t.Skip("POSIX executable fixtures")
   180		}
   181		for _, tt := range []struct {
   182			name, script, version string
   183			success               bool
   184		}{
   185			{"version on stdout", `echo "opencode v2.0.14"`, "opencode v2.0.14", true},
   186			{"version on stderr", `echo "opencode v2.0.14" >&2`, "opencode v2.0.14", true},
   187			{"empty output", "exit 0", "unknown", true},
   188			{"failure", "echo boom >&2; exit 3", "", false},
   189		} {
   190			t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   191				path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "open code")
   192				if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"+tt.script+"\n"), 0o700); err != nil {
   193					t.Fatal(err)
   194				}
   195				command := `"` + path + `" --flag`
   196				result := NewProvider().Check(command)
   197				if result.Success != tt.success || result.Version != tt.version {
   198					t.Fatalf("Check() = %+v", result)
   199				}
   200				if tt.success && result.ErrorType != "" {
   201					t.Errorf("ErrorType on success = %q", result.ErrorType)
   202				}
   203				if !tt.success {
   204					if result.ErrorType == "" || !strings.Contains(result.ErrorMessage, command+" --version") || !strings.Contains(result.ErrorMessage, "boom") {
   205						t.Errorf("failure lost its type, command or stderr: %+v", result)
   206					}
   207				}
   208			})
   209		}
   210	
   211		missing := NewProvider().Check(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "no-such-opencode"))
   212		if missing.Success || missing.ErrorType != spi.CheckErrorNotFound || !strings.Contains(missing.ErrorMessage, "no-such-opencode") {
   213			t.Errorf("missing custom binary = %+v", missing)
   214		}
   215	}

   226			`{"time":{"created":1000},"text":"","files":[{"name":"screenshot.png","mime":"image/png","source":{"type":"file","path":"screenshot.png"},"data":"iVBORw0KGgo="}],"agents":[]}`)

    21	// reconstructionSource is a session with plain turns, thinking and a tool

    24		summary := "Tool use: **shell**"
    25		formatted := "\n```bash\nls\n```\n\nResult:\n\n```text\nhello.py\n```\n"
    26		return &schema.SessionData{
    27			SchemaVersion: schema.CurrentSchemaVersion,
    28			Provider:      schema.ProviderInfo{ID: "claude", Name: "Claude Code", Version: "2.1.0"},
    29			SessionID:     "source-session-id",
    30			CreatedAt:     "2026-09-22T10:00:00Z",
    31			Slug:          "list-the-files",
    32			WorkspaceRoot: "/Users/dev/project",
    33			Exchanges: []schema.Exchange{{
    34				ExchangeID: "e1",
    35				Messages: []schema.Message{
    36					{Role: schema.RoleUser, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "The magic passphrase is PURPLE-ELEPHANT-42. List the files."}}},
    37					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeThinking, Text: "I should run ls."}}},
    38					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Tool: &schema.ToolInfo{Name: "Bash", Type: schema.ToolTypeShell, Summary: &summary, FormattedMarkdown: &formatted}},
    39					{Role: schema.RoleAgent, Content: []schema.ContentPart{{Type: schema.ContentTypeText, Text: "There is one file: hello.py."}}},
    40				},
    41			}},
    42		}

    45	func TestReconstructSession(t *testing.T) {
    46		source := reconstructionSource()
    47		opts := spi.ReconstructOptions{WorkspaceRoot: "/Users/dev/target", MigrationNote: "Resumed from a Claude Code session via SpecStory."}
    48		p := NewProvider()
    49	
    50		rec, err := p.ReconstructSession(source, opts)
    51		if err != nil {
    52			t.Fatal(err)
    53		}
    54		if !openCodeIDPattern.MatchString(rec.SessionID) || !strings.HasPrefix(rec.SessionID, sessionIDPrefix) {
    55			t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, not an OpenCode session id", rec.SessionID)
    56		}
    57		if rec.Filename != rec.SessionID+".json" {
    58			t.Errorf("Filename = %q", rec.Filename)
    59		}
    60	
    61		var document struct {
    62			Info     map[string]any   `json:"info"`
    63			Messages []map[string]any `json:"messages"`
    64		}
    65		if err := json.Unmarshal(rec.Content, &document); err != nil {
    66			t.Fatalf("export document is not JSON: %v", err)
    67		}
    68	
    69		info := document.Info
    70		if info["id"] != rec.SessionID || info["title"] != "list-the-files" {
    71			t.Errorf("info id/title = %v / %v", info["id"], info["title"])
    72		}
    73		if location, _ := info["location"].(map[string]any); location["directory"] != "/Users/dev/target" {
    74			t.Errorf("location = %v, want the target workspace", info["location"])
    75		}
    76		if metadata, _ := info["metadata"].(map[string]any); metadata["specstorySourceSessionId"] != "source-session-id" {
    77			t.Errorf("metadata = %v, want the provenance back-link", info["metadata"])
    78		}
    79		// Required import fields, with neutral values.
    80		for _, field := range []string{"projectID", "cost", "tokens", "time"} {
    81			if _, ok := info[field]; !ok {
    82				t.Errorf("info.%s missing", field)
    83			}
    84		}
    85	
    86		// The records carry the prepared turns verbatim and in order.
    87		turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(source, opts)
    88		if err != nil {
    89			t.Fatal(err)
    90		}
    91		if len(document.Messages) != len(turns) {
    92			t.Fatalf("messages = %d, turns = %d", len(document.Messages), len(turns))
    93		}
    94		var previousCreated float64
    95		seen := map[string]bool{}
    96		for i, message := range document.Messages {
    97			turn := turns[i]
    98			id, _ := message["id"].(string)
    99			if !openCodeIDPattern.MatchString(id) || !strings.HasPrefix(id, messageIDPrefix) || seen[id] {
   100				t.Errorf("message %d id %q invalid or repeated", i, id)
   101			}
   102			seen[id] = true
   103			created, _ := message["time"].(map[string]any)["created"].(float64)
   104			if created <= previousCreated {
   105				t.Errorf("message %d created %v does not follow %v", i, created, previousCreated)
   106			}
   107			previousCreated = created
   108	
   109			if turn.Role == schema.RoleUser {
   110				if message["type"] != recordUser || message["text"] != turn.Text {
   111					t.Errorf("message %d = %v, want user %q", i, message, turn.Text)
   112				}
   113				continue
   114			}
   115			content, _ := message["content"].([]any)
   116			part, _ := content[0].(map[string]any)
   117			if message["type"] != recordAssistant || len(content) != 1 || part["type"] != "text" || part["text"] != turn.Text {
   118				t.Errorf("message %d = %v, want assistant text %q", i, message, turn.Text)
   119			}
   120			if message["agent"] != "" || message["finish"] != "stop" {
   121				t.Errorf("message %d agent/finish = %v / %v", i, message["agent"], message["finish"])
   122			}
   123			if model, _ := message["model"].(map[string]any); model["id"] != "" || model["providerID"] != "" {
   124				t.Errorf("message %d model = %v, want neutral", i, message["model"])
   125			}
   126		}
   127		first, _ := document.Messages[0]["content"].([]any)
   128		if note, _ := first[0].(map[string]any); note["text"] != opts.MigrationNote {
   129			t.Errorf("first record = %v, want the migration note", document.Messages[0])
   130		}
   131		// Thinking and tool activity arrive as ordinary agent text.
   132		if !strings.Contains(string(rec.Content), "I should run ls.") || !strings.Contains(string(rec.Content), "hello.py") {
   133			t.Error("thinking or rendered tool activity missing from the reconstruction")
   134		}
   135	}

   137	// isolateUserCache points the user cache directory at a temp dir on every OS.
   138	func isolateUserCache(t *testing.T) {

   146	func TestReconstructionCapabilityAgrees(t *testing.T) {
   147		isolateUserCache(t)
   148		p := NewProvider()
   149		if !p.SupportsReconstruction() {
   150			t.Fatal("SupportsReconstruction() = false")
   151		}
   152		rec, err := p.ReconstructSession(reconstructionSource(), spi.ReconstructOptions{WorkspaceRoot: "/Users/dev/target"})
   153		if errors.Is(err, spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported) || err != nil {
   154			t.Fatalf("ReconstructSession() error = %v", err)
   155		}
   156		path, err := p.NativeSessionPath("/Users/dev/target", rec.Filename)
   157		if err != nil {
   158			t.Fatalf("NativeSessionPath() error = %v", err)
   159		}
   160		// The resume flow writes the document where ExecAgentAndWatch looks for it.
   161		staged, err := stagedImportPath(stagedImportFilename(rec.SessionID))
   162		if err != nil || path != staged {
   163			t.Errorf("NativeSessionPath() = %q, staged import path = %q (%v)", path, staged, err)
   164		}
   165		// The staged conversation is private to the user.
   166		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
   167			info, err := os.Stat(filepath.Dir(path))
   168			if err != nil {
   169				t.Fatal(err)
   170			}
   171			if info.Mode().Perm() != 0o700 {
   172				t.Errorf("staging directory mode = %v, want 0700", info.Mode().Perm())
   173			}
   174		}
   175	}

   177	func TestNewOpenCodeIDOrdering(t *testing.T) {
   178		early := time.UnixMilli(1790117553306)
   179		late := early.Add(time.Second)
   180	
   181		earlySession := newOpenCodeID(sessionIDPrefix, early, true)
   182		lateSession := newOpenCodeID(sessionIDPrefix, late, true)
   183		// OpenCode's session ids sort newest first.
   184		if lateSession >= earlySession {
   185			t.Errorf("session ids not descending: %s then %s", earlySession, lateSession)
   186		}
   187	
   188		first := newOpenCodeID(messageIDPrefix, late, false)
   189		second := newOpenCodeID(messageIDPrefix, late, false)
   190		if second <= first {
   191			t.Errorf("message ids minted in the same millisecond not ascending: %s then %s", first, second)
   192		}
   193		// The layout matches an id OpenCode 2.0.14 minted at the same time.
   194		if got := newOpenCodeID(sessionIDPrefix, early, true)[:16]; got[:12] != "ses_f34addb6" {
   195			t.Errorf("session id prefix = %s, want ses_f34addb6... like OpenCode's", got)
   196		}
   197	}

   199	// fakeOpenCode installs a script that records its arguments, one per line.
   200	func fakeOpenCode(t *testing.T, exitCode string) (command, argsFile string) {
   201		t.Helper()
   202		if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
   203			t.Skip("POSIX executable fixtures")
   204		}
   205		dir := t.TempDir()
   206		argsFile = filepath.Join(dir, "args.txt")
   207		command = filepath.Join(dir, "opencode")
   208		script := "#!/bin/sh\nfor a in \"$@\"; do echo \"$a\" >> '" + argsFile + "'; done\necho imported\nexit " + exitCode + "\n"
   209		if err := os.WriteFile(command, []byte(script), 0o700); err != nil {
   210			t.Fatal(err)
   211		}
   212		return command, argsFile
   213	}

   293	func TestExecuteOpenCodeResumeArguments(t *testing.T) {
   294		for _, tt := range []struct {
   295			name, custom, resume string
   296			want                 []string
   297			exitCode             string
   298		}{
   299			{name: "resume adds the session flag", resume: "ses_new", want: []string{"--session", "ses_new"}, exitCode: "0"},
   300			{name: "requested session replaces a pinned one", custom: "-s ses_pinned --auto", resume: "ses_new", want: []string{"-s", "ses_new", "--auto"}, exitCode: "0"},
   301			{name: "no resume keeps the configured arguments", custom: "--auto", want: []string{"--auto"}, exitCode: "0"},
   302			{name: "non-zero exit is the agent's status", exitCode: "7"},
   303		} {
   304			t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   305				command, argsFile := fakeOpenCode(t, tt.exitCode)
   306				err := executeOpenCode(strings.TrimSpace(command+" "+tt.custom), t.TempDir(), tt.resume)
   307				if tt.exitCode != "0" {
   308					var exitErr *spi.AgentExitError
   309					if !errors.As(err, &exitErr) || exitErr.Code != 7 {
   310						t.Fatalf("executeOpenCode() error = %v, want AgentExitError 7", err)
   311					}
   312					return
   313				}
   314				if err != nil {
   315					t.Fatal(err)
   316				}
   317				args, _ := os.ReadFile(argsFile)
   318				if got := strings.Fields(string(args)); strings.Join(got, " ") != strings.Join(tt.want, " ") {
   319					t.Errorf("args = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
   320				}
   321			})
   322		}
   323	}

    17	// fastWatcherTiming shortens the watcher's intervals for the test.
    18	func fastWatcherTiming(t *testing.T) {
    19		t.Helper()
    20		debounce, burst, reconcile := debounceDelay, maxBurstDelay, reconcileInterval
    21		debounceDelay, maxBurstDelay, reconcileInterval = 20*time.Millisecond, 100*time.Millisecond, 150*time.Millisecond
    22		t.Cleanup(func() {
    23			debounceDelay, maxBurstDelay, reconcileInterval = debounce, burst, reconcile
    24		})
    25	}
    26	
    27	// deliveries records what the watcher delivers.
    28	type deliveries struct {
    29		mu       sync.Mutex
    30		sessions []*spi.AgentChatSession
    31	}
    32	
    33	func (d *deliveries) callback(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
    34		d.mu.Lock()
    35		defer d.mu.Unlock()
    36		d.sessions = append(d.sessions, session)
    37	}
    38	
    39	func (d *deliveries) ids() []string {
    40		d.mu.Lock()
    41		defer d.mu.Unlock()
    42		var ids []string
    43		for _, session := range d.sessions {
    44			ids = append(ids, session.SessionID)
    45		}
    46		return ids
    47	}
    48	
    49	func (d *deliveries) count() int {
    50		d.mu.Lock()
    51		defer d.mu.Unlock()
    52		return len(d.sessions)
    53	}
    54	
    55	// waitFor polls until condition holds or the deadline passes.
    56	func waitFor(t *testing.T, condition func() bool) bool {
    57		t.Helper()
    58		deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
    59		for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
    60			if condition() {
    61				return true
    62			}
    63			time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
    64		}
    65		return condition()
    66	}
    67	
    68	// quietPeriod is long enough for several reconciliation passes.
    69	func quietPeriod() { time.Sleep(4 * reconcileInterval) }
    70	
    71	// writeSession writes a session with one prompt and one reply, stamped at ms.
    72	func writeSession(t *testing.T, db *sql.DB, id, project string, ms int64) {
    73		t.Helper()
    74		insertSession(t, db, id, project, ms, ms)
    75		insertMessage(t, db, id, id+"_u", recordUser, 1, ms, userData(ms, "prompt for "+id))
    76		insertMessage(t, db, id, id+"_a", recordAssistant, 2, ms, assistantData(ms, "reply for "+id))
    77	}
    78	
    79	// appendReply adds a reply to an existing session, stamped now, in one
    80	// transaction so the watcher sees it as a single change.
    81	func appendReply(t *testing.T, db *sql.DB, id string, seq int64, text string) {
    82		t.Helper()
    83		now := time.Now().UnixMilli()
    84		tx, err := db.Begin()
    85		if err != nil {
    86			t.Fatal(err)
    87		}
    88		if _, err := tx.Exec(`INSERT INTO session_message (id, session_id, type, seq, time_created, time_updated, data)
    89			VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`, id+"_"+text, id, recordAssistant, seq, now, now, assistantData(now, text)); err != nil {
    90			t.Fatal(err)
    91		}
    92		if _, err := tx.Exec(`UPDATE session_v2 SET time_updated = ? WHERE id = ?`, now, id); err != nil {
    93			t.Fatal(err)
    94		}
    95		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
    96			t.Fatal(err)
    97		}
    98	}

   100	func hourAgo() int64 { return time.Now().Add(-time.Hour).UnixMilli() }
   101	
   102	func TestWatcherLeavesUnchangedSessionsAloneAtStartup(t *testing.T) {
   103		fastWatcherTiming(t)
   104		project := newProjectDir(t, "project")
   105		db := createFixtureDB(t, useFixtureStore(t))
   106		writeSession(t, db, "ses_existing", project, hourAgo())
   107	
   108		var got deliveries
   109		w, err := startWatcher(project, false, got.callback)
   110		if err != nil {
   111			t.Fatal(err)
   112		}
   113		quietPeriod()
   114		w.Stop()
   115	
   116		if got.count() != 0 {
   117			t.Errorf("delivered %v for a session written before startup", got.ids())
   118		}
   119	}

   121	func TestWatcherEmitsActivityDuringStartup(t *testing.T) {
   122		fastWatcherTiming(t)
   123		project := newProjectDir(t, "project")
   124		db := createFixtureDB(t, useFixtureStore(t))
   125		writeSession(t, db, "ses_existing", project, hourAgo())
   126	
   127		// Activity lands after the watch exists but before the first read.
   128		beforeFirstCheck = func() {
   129			appendReply(t, db, "ses_existing", 3, "during-startup")
   130			writeSession(t, db, "ses_new", project, time.Now().UnixMilli())
   131		}
   132		t.Cleanup(func() { beforeFirstCheck = nil })
   133	
   134		var got deliveries
   135		w, err := startWatcher(project, false, got.callback)
   136		if err != nil {
   137			t.Fatal(err)
   138		}
   139		defer w.Stop()
   140	
   141		if !waitFor(t, func() bool { return got.count() >= 2 }) {
   142			t.Fatalf("delivered %v, want both sessions changed during startup", got.ids())
   143		}
   144	}

   146	func TestWatcherAdoptsStoreCreatedAfterStartup(t *testing.T) {
   147		fastWatcherTiming(t)
   148		project := newProjectDir(t, "project")
   149		dbPath := useFixtureStore(t)
   150		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Dir(dbPath)); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   151			t.Fatalf("data directory exists before startup: %v", err)
   152		}
   153	
   154		var got deliveries
   155		w, err := startWatcher(project, false, got.callback)
   156		if err != nil {
   157			t.Fatalf("watcher must wait for a missing store, got %v", err)
   158		}
   159		defer w.Stop()
   160	
   161		// The store arrives after startup carrying a session with old timestamps
   162		// (restored or copied into place); arrival is activity.
   163		db := createFixtureDB(t, dbPath)
   164		writeSession(t, db, "ses_restored", project, hourAgo())
   165	
   166		if !waitFor(t, func() bool { return got.count() == 1 }) {
   167			t.Fatalf("delivered %v, want the session in the late store", got.ids())
   168		}
   169	}

   172	// after startup began but before the watcher's first read: it arrived after
   173	// startup, so its sessions are adopted even though their timestamps are old.
   174	func TestWatcherAdoptsStoreRestoredDuringStartup(t *testing.T) {

+// formatInputSchema lists a tool's parameters, required ones first, with their
+// types and descriptions.
+func formatInputSchema(schema map[string]any) string {
+	if schema == nil {
+		return "Parameters: none"
+	}
+	var b strings.Builder
+	properties, _ := schema["properties"].(map[string]any)
+	if len(properties) == 0 {
+		b.WriteString("Parameters: none")
+	} else {
+		b.WriteString("Parameters:\n")
+		writeSchemaProperties(&b, schema, 0)
+	}
+	// Keys such as additionalProperties constrain the whole input; "type" is
+	// always "object" for a tool input and says nothing.
+	if extra := formatParameters(withoutKeys(schema, "type", "properties", "required")); extra != "" {
+		b.WriteString("\n\n" + extra)
+	}
+	return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
+}
+
+// writeSchemaProperties writes one bullet per property of an object schema,
+// nesting the properties of object and array-of-object parameters beneath it.
+func writeSchemaProperties(b *strings.Builder, schema map[string]any, depth int) {
+	properties, _ := schema["properties"].(map[string]any)
+	required, _ := stringList(schema["required"])
+	names := make([]string, 0, len(properties))
+	for name := range properties {
+		names = append(names, name)
+	}
+	sort.SliceStable(names, func(i, j int) bool {
+		iRequired, jRequired := slices.Contains(required, names[i]), slices.Contains(required, names[j])
+		if iRequired != jRequired {
+			return iRequired
+		}
+		return names[i] < names[j]
+	})
+
+	indent := strings.Repeat("  ", depth)
+	for _, name := range names {
+		property, ok := properties[name].(map[string]any)
+		if !ok {
+			fmt.Fprintf(b, "%s- %s: %s\n", indent, codeSpan(name), codeSpan(stringArg(properties, name)))
+			continue
+		}
+		var qualifiers []string
+		if schemaType := schemaTypeName(property); schemaType != "" {
+			qualifiers = append(qualifiers, schemaType)
+		}
+		if slices.Contains(required, name) {
+			qualifiers = append(qualifiers, "required")
+		}
+		line := indent + "- " + codeSpan(name)
+		if len(qualifiers) > 0 {
+			line += " (" + strings.Join(qualifiers, ", ") + ")"
+		}
+		// A description can span paragraphs; one line keeps the list intact.
+		if description := strings.Join(strings.Fields(stringArg(property, "description")), " "); description != "" {
+			line += ": " + description
+		}
+		if values, ok := property["enum"].([]any); ok && len(values) > 0 {
+			spans := make([]string, 0, len(values))
+			for _, value := range values {
+				spans = append(spans, codeSpan(jsonText(value)))
+			}
+			line += " One of: " + strings.Join(spans, ", ") + "."
+		}
+		consumed := []string{"type", "anyOf", "oneOf", "description", "enum", "properties", "required"}
+		items, _ := property["items"].(map[string]any)
+		if schemaTypeName(property) != "" {
+			consumed = append(consumed, "items")
+		}
+		for _, key := range sortedKeys(withoutKeys(property, consumed...)) {
+			line += fmt.Sprintf("; %s: %s", key, codeSpan(jsonText(property[key])))
+		}
+		b.WriteString(line + "\n")
+
+		if _, nested := property["properties"].(map[string]any); nested {
+			writeSchemaProperties(b, property, depth+1)
+		} else if _, nested := items["properties"].(map[string]any); nested {
+			writeSchemaProperties(b, items, depth+1)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// schemaTypeName describes a JSON schema's type the way a reader would say it:
+// "string", "array of string", "string | null".
+func schemaTypeName(schema map[string]any) string {
+	switch typed := schema["type"].(type) {
+	case string:
+		if items, ok := schema["items"].(map[string]any); typed == "array" && ok {
+			if itemType := schemaTypeName(items); itemType != "" {
+				return "array of " + itemType
+			}
+		}
+		return typed
+	case []any:
+		if names, ok := stringList(typed); ok {
+			return strings.Join(names, " | ")
+		}
+	}
+	for _, key := range []string{"anyOf", "oneOf"} {
+		branches, ok := schema[key].([]any)
+		if !ok {
+			continue
+		}
+		var names []string
+		for _, raw := range branches {
+			branch, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
+			if !ok {
+				return ""
+			}
+			name := schemaTypeName(branch)
+			if name == "" {
+				return ""
+			}
+			names = append(names, name)
+		}
+		return strings.Join(names, " | ")
+	}
+	return ""
+}
+
+// formatTaskEnvelope turns the tagged envelope Grok returns for a backgrounded
+// command (<task-id>, <status>, <output-file>, ...) into labeled lines. It
+// returns "" for any output that does not open with that envelope.
+func formatTaskEnvelope(text string) string {
+	if !strings.HasPrefix(text, "<task-id>") {
+		return ""
+	}
+	var fields, rest []string
+	for _, line := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
+		match := taskEnvelopeTagRe.FindStringSubmatch(line)
+		if match == nil || match[1] != match[3] {
+			rest = append(rest, line)
+			continue
+		}
+		fields = append(fields, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", tagLabel(match[1]), codeSpan(match[2])))
+	}
+	result := strings.Join(fields, "\n")
+	if remaining := strings.TrimSpace(strings.Join(rest, "\n")); remaining != "" {
+		result += "\n\n" + fenceIfMultiline(remaining)
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+var taskEnvelopeTagRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^<([a-z][a-z-]*)>(.*)</([a-z][a-z-]*)>$`)
+

+// tagLabel turns a native tag such as "output-file" into "Output file".
+func tagLabel(tag string) string {
+	words := strings.Split(tag, "-")
+	for i, word := range words {
+		if word == "id" {
+			words[i] = "ID"
+		}
+	}
+	label := strings.Join(words, " ")
+	return strings.ToUpper(label[:1]) + label[1:]
+}
+
+// formatImageResult shows where a generated or edited image was saved. Grok
+// returns a JSON envelope whose message repeats the path alongside an
+// instruction to the model not to describe the image, and whose filename and
+// folder are both parts of the path; the path alone says it all. It returns ""
+// when the result is not that envelope.
+func formatImageResult(text string) string {
+	var envelope map[string]any
+	if !looksLikeJSON(text) || json.Unmarshal([]byte(text), &envelope) != nil {
+		return ""
+	}
+	path, _ := envelope["path"].(string)
+	if path == "" {
+		return ""
+	}
+	result := fmt.Sprintf("Saved image: %s", codeSpan(path))
+	if extra := formatParameters(withoutKeys(envelope, "path", "filename", "session_folder", "message")); extra != "" {
+		result += "\n" + extra
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+// stripWorkspaceWrapper removes the <workspace_result> tags Grok wraps search
+// output in. They only restate the session's workspace, and left bare they
+// read as markup in the middle of the results.
+func stripWorkspaceWrapper(text string) string {
+	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(text)
+	if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<workspace_result") || !strings.HasSuffix(trimmed, "</workspace_result>") {
+		return text
+	}
+	opening, body, found := strings.Cut(trimmed, "\n")
+	if !found || !strings.HasSuffix(opening, ">") {
+		return text
+	}
+	return strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(body, "</workspace_result>"))
+}
+
+// resultText is a tool's output with Grok's trailing "
+	stripped := text
+	for strings.HasSuffix(strings.TrimRight(stripped, " \t\r\n"), closeTag) {
+		start := strings.LastIndex(stripped, openTag)
+		if start < 0 {
+			break
+		}
+		stripped = stripped[:start]
+	}
+	if stripped == text {
+		return text
+	}
+	// Only the separator Grok puts before the reminder is removed.
+	return strings.TrimRight(stripped, " \t\r\n")
+}

+// stringList reads a JSON array whose items are all strings. The bool is false
+// for any other value, so a caller can fall back to rendering it as JSON.
+func stringList(value any) ([]string, bool) {
+	switch typed := value.(type) {
+	case []string:
+		return typed, true
+	case []any:
+		items := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
+		for _, raw := range typed {
+			item, ok := raw.(string)
+			if !ok {
+				return nil, false
+			}
+			items = append(items, item)
+		}
+		return items, true
+	}
+	return nil, false
+}
+
+// withoutKeys returns a copy of m without the named keys, leaving m intact.
+func withoutKeys(m map[string]any, keys ...string) map[string]any {
+	kept := make(map[string]any, len(m))
+	for key, value := range m {
+		if !slices.Contains(keys, key) {
+			kept[key] = value
+		}
+	}
+	return kept
+}
+
+func sortedKeys(m map[string]any) []string {
+	keys := make([]string, 0, len(m))
+	for key := range m {
+		keys = append(keys, key)
+	}
+	sort.Strings(keys)
+	return keys
+}
+
+// jsonText renders a JSON value as its literal text: strings as-is, everything
+// else encoded, including null.
+func jsonText(value any) string {
+	if text, ok := value.(string); ok {
+		return text
+	}
+	encoded, err := json.Marshal(value)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Sprint(value)
+	}
+	return string(encoded)
+}
+
+// codeSpan wraps text in an inline code span whose backtick run is longer than
+// any inside the text, so tool descriptions and schema values that contain
+// backticks cannot break out of the span.
+func codeSpan(text string) string {
+	if !strings.Contains(text, "`") {
+		return "`" + text + "`"
+	}
+	longest, run := 0, 0
+	for _, r := range text {
+		if r == '`' {
+			run++
+			longest = max(longest, run)
+		} else {
+			run = 0
+		}
+	}
+	fence := strings.Repeat("`", longest+1)
+	// CommonMark strips one space from each side, which lets the span start or
+	// end with a backtick.
+	return fence + " " + text + " " + fence
+}
+
+// headerText fits text to one line of a collapsed summary, marking a cut.
+func headerText(text string, maxRunes int) string {
+	line := strings.Join(strings.Fields(text), " ")
+	count := 0
+	for i := range line {
+		if count == maxRunes {
+			return strings.TrimRight(line[:i], " ") + "…"
+		}
+		count++
+	}
+	return line
+}
+
+// formatTextBlock fences a free-text argument such as a prompt, which is
+// often long and may span lines.
+func formatTextBlock(label, text string) string {
+	if text == "" {
+		return ""
+	}
+	return fmt.Sprintf("%s:\n%s", label, spi.CodeFence("text", text))
+}

+func workflowName(input map[string]any) string {

+	if name := stringArg(source, "name"); name != "" {
+		return name
+	}
+	if match := workflowMetaNameRe.FindStringSubmatch(stringArg(source, "script")); match != nil {
+		return match[1]

+// formatWorkflowBody shows a workflow's source: a saved workflow by name, or an
+// inline Rhai script in full.
+func formatWorkflowBody(input map[string]any) string {
+	raw, present := input["source"]
+	if !present {
+		return ""
+	}
+	source, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
+	if !ok {
+		return formatParameters(map[string]any{"source": raw})

+	var parts []string
+	if _, ok := source["type"]; ok {
+		parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("Source: %s", codeSpan(stringArg(source, "type"))))
+	}
+	if extra := formatParameters(withoutKeys(source, "type", "script")); extra != "" {
+		parts = append(parts, extra)

+	for _, field := range []struct{ key, label string }{{"title", "Title"}, {"type", "Type"}} {

+		parts = append(parts, "\n"+details)
+	}
+	return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
